status: Draft: one design per realm of the roster of 24 October 2026 (156 realms, real tags); every design is proposed and provisional until the owner reviews the sheets
note: Grammars per culture and people, family marks, one design record per realm of roster.json (156 realms, keyed by key and tag), the dynamic-tag derivation and fallback designs, the forbidden register and the build checks. Hex values are the design tinctures; the palette-fit check measures generated images against them. The countries section, the new grammars and the renames are written by the generator; edit its tables, not this file.

lines.stepped: a stepped line like a short stair (grady)
lines.nebuly: a cloud-like interlocking line (nebuly), like a cord pulled through loops
lines.engrailed: an engrailed line of small inward scallops
lines.invected: an invected line of small outward scallops
lines.rayonny: a rayonny line of alternating straight and flame-shaped rays
lines.raguly: a raguly line of lopped-branch stubs
lines.dovetailed: a dovetailed line of joiner's mortises
lines.potenty: a potenty line of T-shaped notches
lines.bevilled: a bevilled line with a single sharp offset step
lines.double_arched: two low arches side by side
lines.dancetty: a dancetty line of three large zigzag peaks
lines.urdy: an urdy line of pointed stakes
lines.rooted: a rooted line from which short root-strands hang
lines.rent: a rent line, jagged like torn hide
lines.fracted: a fracted line, broken and offset halfway along
lines.escartelly: an escartelly line with one square notch
lines.gnarled: a gnarled line of slow, uneven swellings like old bark
lines.gilled: a gilled line of fine close upright ribs, like the underside of a mushroom cap
lines.wattled: a wattled line woven over and under like a hurdle of branches

tincture_rule: A tincture is a metal when its relative luminance exceeds 0.30, otherwise a colour. Charges sit metal on colour or colour on metal (luminance ratio at least 2.2), or are fimbriated.

ainic_men.name: Ainic men
ainic_men.mark_text: Aen's label: a narrow bar across the upper field with three short square pendants, in a metal of the culture
ainic_men.meaning: The label is the medieval mark of a son of the house. Realms of Ainic speech and stock bear it because their first crowns were among the kingdoms Aen joined, and the Reckoning of Lines counts their founding houses among the descendants of his sons (proposed reading). Aenor itself bears none: the crown of Aen's own realm needs no difference. A theocracy bears none, because a faith claims no line.

boreal_men.name: Boreal men
boreal_men.mark_text: every line of partition is indented: small even teeth
boreal_men.meaning: The indented line is the toothed north-western shore that the Aenoran charts met already peopled; Gunwyn, Coldic and Tritonic realms all draw it, which is how a Triton chart-house and a Cold Lands clan show they share a stock older than the charts.

eastern_men.name: Eastern men
eastern_men.mark_text: every line of partition is stepped like a temple stair (grady); never crenellated
eastern_men.meaning: The stepped line is the stair: the temple stairs above the flood-line, the terraced roads of the caravans and the wells cut in steps. Noric, Stabilic and Alerhic realms all draw it, from the snow coast of Woqood to the passes of Miaed and the wells of Wahatud; the line marks the stock, and each realm keeps its own faith.

orran_men.name: Orran men
orran_men.mark_text: every line is nebuly, like a cord drawn through loops
orran_men.meaning: The nebuly line is the cord of the Old Knots, the oldest custom of men in Aoaz, kept by the speech of the beaten kingdoms.

yonic_men.name: Southern islanders
yonic_men.meaning: The wavy line is the reef's surf, counted wave by wave in the Wave-Tally.

sun_patronage.name: Men under Sunhot patronage
sun_patronage.mark_text: a chief whose lower edge is rayonny, in sun yellow
sun_patronage.meaning: Men who serve the Sunhot sanctuaries carry the patrons' rayonny edge only on a chief: the sanctuary stands over the guest-town, it is not its kin.

sylvan_elves.name: Sylvan elves
sylvan_elves.mark_text: every line is engrailed, and elven silver appears in every achievement
sylvan_elves.meaning: The engrailed line is the edge of a leaf; silver is the Kindred Song. The realms of the Magical Lands and the household of Dunelaeth on the wrong side of the range share both, so a hill hall and a lake court are known as kin at a glance.

galic_elves.name: Gala elves
galic_elves.meaning: The invected line is the rim of the Mirror of First Rain. It is deliberately not the Sunhot rayonny line: the kinship of Gala and the Sunhot realms is open, and the arms must not answer it.

sunhot_elves.name: Sunhot elves
sunhot_elves.mark_text: every line is rayonny; a sun disc appears in at most one achievement of each culture
sunhot_elves.meaning: The rayonny line is noon light on a sanctuary threshold. It carries the Sunhot identity so that the charges are free to show what each sanctuary keeps, instead of a sun on every banner.

orcish.name: Orcs and ogres
orcish.mark_text: every line is raguly, like a lopped branch
orcish.meaning: The raguly line is the hewn stake of the holds' palisades and the challenge ring; every hold draws it, which says the holds are kin without saying they obey one master. Ogres draw it too, because an ogre is like a giant orc and lives among them.

goblin.name: Goblins
goblin.mark_text: every line is potenty, like tunnel mouths
goblin.meaning: The potenty line is a warren seen in section: tunnel, chamber, tunnel. The free warrens of Burnikit, the hobgoblin king's warrens of Burrikkrit and the warm-spring warrens of Glimkit all draw it.

dwarven.name: Dwarves
dwarven.mark_text: every line is dovetailed, like a joiner's mortise cut true into rock
dwarven.meaning: The dovetailed line is a hall cut true into the mountain. The hold-folks of the Great Wall range, the West Lands and the High Mountains all draw it, and no tincture of theirs is shared with any elven arms.

isolate.name: Peoples without kin
isolate.mark_text: each people keeps its own line (see the people grammar)
isolate.meaning: Trolls, giants, yeti, ents, the Baelim, the mycids, the small folk, the gnomes, the dwarf goblins, the God Forest Keepers, the dead and the demons share no line with anyone outside their people: their arms answer only their own people.

peoples.name: Men

peoples.line: by family (Ainic straight with the label, Boreal indented, Eastern stepped, Orran nebuly, Yonic wavy)
peoples.ornament: Plain edges; crowns drawn as circlets of the culture; beasts walk or stand, never rampant in a lion-of-a-national-arms pose.
peoples.rank: Monarchies wear the culture crown over the primary charge; councils and leagues wear none; subjects take their overlord's mark.
peoples.kinship: Through the five family lines; mixed realms borrow one tincture or one secondary charge of their second culture.

peoples.name: Elves (Great Folk)

peoples.ornament: Silver in every achievement; long, drawn-out charges; no crown of points, only a leaf circlet for the few hill queens and kings.
peoples.rank: Elected speakers wear an engrailed silver border; a hall-crowned queen or king wears the leaf circlet; leagues of house-towers triple their charge.
peoples.kinship: Sylvan cultures share the engrailed line and silver; Gala keeps its own invected line because its relation to the Sunhot elves is open.

peoples.name: Sunhot elves
peoples.status: culture entries exist
peoples.ornament: Tall, narrow charges (the Sunhot stand over three metres); no weapons, because no weapon passes a sanctuary door.
peoples.rank: No Sunhot realm is a kingdom: elders are never called kings. A Speaker's realm is shown by a sanctuary-white field part; the Lands of Light alone may bear the noon-door.
peoples.kinship: The rayonny line. Men under Sunhot patronage carry it on a chief only.

peoples.kinship: None: the two realms of the dead share no device, because their relation is open.

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the charter border: a plain narrow border of lamp gold, the seal-cord of the Charters of Parim

countries.meaning: Freshon bears the barley of its four states of spring country under a chief of pale gold, with the hanging gold seal of the Golden Charter it bought in 4A 1731: a proud spring-town whose loyalty the Golden Court holds by its debts.
countries.blazon: A field of lake blue with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of pale gold edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in deep lake. A sheaf of barley in Parim white, large in the field below the chief. A hanging gold seal on a cord in lamp gold, small, beneath it. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Pazoma

primary_charge.name: a lake-glass flask
primary_charge.meaning: the glassworks of the shore towns

secondary_charge.name: a quill
secondary_charge.meaning: the scribes who keep the rolls and the charters

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the charter border: a plain narrow border of lamp gold, the seal-cord of the Charters of Parim

countries.meaning: Pazoma bears the flask of its lake-glass and the quill of its paper-makers and copyists: the guild-city of the deep bay that has never had a lord and makes the Concord's bells, glass, cloth, paper and books.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper fly corner, deep lake above and pale gold below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in Parim white. A lake-glass flask in Parim white, outlined in deep lake, large in the centre. A quill in bell bronze, small, beneath it. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Orohaf

primary_charge.name: a lighthouse with a red fire
primary_charge.meaning: the lighthouse-shrines where the tide-houses name their dead

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the oar-crown: a circlet of five oar-blades
the charter border: a plain narrow border of lamp gold, the seal-cord of the Charters of Parim

countries.meaning: Orohaf bears the lighthouse-shrine of Borrak under the oar-crown of the queen the eldest women of the five Isle Houses choose for life: the harbour every fleet from the West must pass, where the dead are given to the tide.
countries.blazon: A field of foam white with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of sea grey edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in deep sea. A lighthouse with a red fire in sash red, large, standing on the base. Above the charge a circlet of five oar-blades in sash red. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Selen

primary_charge.name: a hollow oak with its roots
primary_charge.meaning: the Moot Tree, and the dead buried standing in hollow oaks

secondary_charge.name: three arrows, points down
secondary_charge.meaning: the Three Arrows: the bride-gift, the poacher's fine and the midsummer shooting

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the charter border: a plain narrow border of lamp gold, the seal-cord of the Charters of Parim

countries.meaning: Selen bears the Moot Tree with the Three Arrows of the Quiet Law beneath it: the woodland moots that elect a First Warden under the oak, once hid a king for two winters and still write their own birth rolls inside the Concord.
countries.blazon: A plain field of wood green. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in birch white. A hollow oak with its roots in birch white, large in the centre. Three arrows, points down in hazel gold, small, beneath it. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Kingson

primary_charge.name: a large key
primary_charge.meaning: the Pass Charter: the key of the only wheel road through the range, held by the Pass-Lord in the crown's name

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the charter border: a plain narrow border of lamp gold, the seal-cord of the Charters of Parim

countries.meaning: Kingson's key lies beneath the snow peaks of the Great Wall of Aenor: the Pass-Lord's charter over the only wheel road through the range, whose tolls are the elves' oldest complaint.
countries.placement: on the lower part of the field
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, snowline white above and vale slate below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in granite. A large key in pass gold, large on the lower part of the field. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Klungori Guard

primary_charge.name: a crossbow
primary_charge.meaning: the crossbows of the sworn pass companies

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the charter border: a plain narrow border of lamp gold, the seal-cord of the Charters of Parim

countries.meaning: The Klungori Guard bears the crossbow of its sworn watch on the rising peak of the South Pass: a garrison company that took land instead of pay to watch the goblin warrens for ever, and whose posts pass from parent to eldest child.
countries.blazon: A field of lichen green with a reversed pile (a broad wedge rising from the bottom edge to a point near the top) of snowline white edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in snowline white. A crossbow in granite, on the reversed pile. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Hirolon

primary_charge.name: a great cairn
primary_charge.meaning: a stone for every year of a giant's life; the cairns are the giants' memory

countries.meaning: Hirolon raises the Eldest Cairn on its arched hill over the green of the Grano that its Hilofrim tenants graze: a sovereign giants' kingdom that treats with Aenor under the Cairn Treaty from outside the Charters and asks only to be left alone.
countries.blazon: A field of Grano green with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of deep earth edged by a single broad arch (enarched). A great cairn in chalk, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Tirlan

primary_charge.name: a round-bellied grain ship with a patched square sail
primary_charge.meaning: the Aenoran grain ship that carried the first households of Tirlan south to the Hilorn mouth

marks.text: Hirolon's ward: a narrow border of cairn brown, the giants who guard every way in

countries.meaning: Tirlan bears the grain ship that blew its first households south to the Hilorn mouth, riding above the double-arched hills of its three valleys, inside the cairn-brown border of the giants who guard every way in.
countries.blazon: A field of harvest yellow with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of basin green edged by two low arches side by side. A round-bellied grain ship with a patched square sail in hearth brown, large, standing on the base. A plain narrow border of cairn brown.

countries.name: Konori

primary_charge.name: a horse's head
primary_charge.meaning: the oath sworn on a horse and carried to the sky

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the white felt: the charge set upon a spread white felt, as kings are acclaimed
the charter border: a plain narrow border of lamp gold, the seal-cord of the Charters of Parim

countries.meaning: Konori's horse's head rests on the white felt on which every king of the Hundreds is lifted at the ford of the Aenar: a riders' kingdom that breeds the Concord's remounts and is paid for them in titles.
countries.blazon: A plain field of steppe red. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in felt white. A horse's head in black felt, large in the centre. The charge rests on a spread felt cloth in felt white. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Hunhun

primary_charge.name: a horse-tail standard on a pole
primary_charge.meaning: the standard of the summer Gathering

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
three small hoof-marks in base: the host
the charter border: a plain narrow border of lamp gold, the seal-cord of the Charters of Parim

countries.meaning: Hunhun bears the horse-tail standard of the midsummer Gathering where its Horse-Lord is chosen, with the hoof-marks of the host beneath it: the first riders to swear to the One Crown, and the largest horse fair in Aoaz.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, felt white above and steppe red below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in black felt. A horse-tail standard on a pole in black felt, large in the centre. In base three small hoof-marks in black felt. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Herez

primary_charge.name: a beacon: a fire-basket on a pole
primary_charge.meaning: the beacon towers of the frontier farms

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the charter border: a plain narrow border of lamp gold, the seal-cord of the Charters of Parim

countries.meaning: Herez lights the beacon of the march Edran set across the Grey Hills so that the remnants of Volgan's host could never again come up the southern road unseen: the realm that will feel the south first, and the only one that expects to.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, chalk white above and palisade brown below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in palisade brown. A beacon: a fire-basket on a pole in beacon red, outlined in chalk white, large in the centre. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Noleksun

primary_charge.name: a ploughshare
primary_charge.meaning: free farmers who own their land

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the charter border: a plain narrow border of lamp gold, the seal-cord of the Charters of Parim

countries.meaning: Noleksun's three ploughshares are the three leagues of free farmers whose eight market towns swore the Oath of Eight Hearths at Saelori: the richest of the frontier dominions, with a Chief Speaker chosen by every hearth.
countries.blazon: A field of field green with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of march ochre edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in chalk white. Three of ploughshare, two above one in chalk white, large, standing on the base. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Kilinti

primary_charge.name: an ancient tree with spreading roots
primary_charge.meaning: the Eldest, who speaks last

marks.text: the charter border: a plain narrow border of lamp gold, the seal-cord of the Charters of Parim

countries.meaning: Kilinti bears the Eldest with its roots spread over a rooted base: a forest whose ent-moot takes years to say a sentence, while the men of its edges keep its accounts and its charter with Parim.
countries.blazon: A field of deep grove with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of bark umber edged by a rooted line from which short root-strands hang. An ancient tree with spreading roots in moss pale, large, standing on the base. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Fotan

primary_charge.name: a chain stretched fesswise from edge to edge
primary_charge.meaning: the chain Ostvar's house stretched across the narrowest landing of the strait

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Fotan stretches its chain across the strait as Ostvar's house first did at the narrowest landing: a free toll-lordship that sealed no charter of Parim and can open or shut the shortest crossing between the North Lands and Aenor.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, quay white above and toll blue below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in tar black. A chain stretched fesswise from edge to edge in chain red, outlined in quay white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Kunhrim

primary_charge.name: a squared gate cut into a rock face
primary_charge.meaning: the Western Gate the clans cut into the Lunhrim massif to trade with Aen's kingdom

secondary_charge.name: a powder horn
secondary_charge.meaning: the black powder the hold sells to the crown and nobody else

marks.text: the charter border: a plain narrow border of lamp gold, the seal-cord of the Charters of Parim

countries.meaning: Kunhrim bears the Western Gate cut into the Lunhrim massif under a dovetailed chief of the range's stone, with the horn of the black powder it sells to the crown and nobody else: the hold of the Iron Charter, which can starve any ruler in Parim of iron.
countries.blazon: A field of delving brown with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of stone grey edged by a dovetailed line of joiner's mortises. A squared gate cut into a rock face in anvil gold, large in the field below the chief. A powder horn in lamp white, small, beneath it. A plain narrow border of lamp gold.

countries.name: Burrikkrit

primary_charge.name: a tunnel mouth under a mountain peak
primary_charge.meaning: the under-roads, the one hidden way through the range, which the king sells in war

secondary_charge.name: a fire-pot with a burning fuse
secondary_charge.meaning: the crude powder thrown in the tunnel fights

marks.text: the grown crown: a goblin crown too small for its wearer

countries.meaning: Burrikkrit bears the tunnel mouth under the peak, its hidden way through the range, under the too-small crown of its hobgoblin king, with the fire-pot of the tunnel fights: a warren-kingdom held to the Lamp Truce that sells its under-roads in war.
countries.blazon: A field of deep moss with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of pit black edged by a potenty line of T-shaped notches. A tunnel mouth under a mountain peak in salvage gold, large, standing on the base. A fire-pot with a burning fuse in fire-pot orange, small, beneath it. Above the charge a small goblin crown, too small for its wearer, in salvage gold.

countries.name: Olodor

primary_charge.name: a pot brimming with gold
primary_charge.meaning: a gnome is crowned when his pot is full; a gift of gold brings luck

marks.text: an orle of lake blue: held inside the land of Aenor

countries.meaning: Olodor's pot of gold stands inside an orle of Aenor's lake blue: hidden holts within a day's walk of Parim, whose village-kings are crowned when their pots are full and whose luck goes to whoever brings them gold freely.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, holt green above and root brown below, by an escartelly line with one square notch. A pot brimming with gold in pot gold, large in the centre. An orle (a narrow inner frame set in from the edges) of lake blue.

countries.name: Dunelaeth

primary_charge.name: a beech in full leaf over a low grassed mound
primary_charge.meaning: the household that would not leave the forests where its dead lay

secondary_charge.name: a silver road winding up to a pass between two hills
secondary_charge.meaning: the road to the Kingson Pass that the household guides travellers on

countries.meaning: Dunelaeth bears the beech that kept its leaves over the road to the Kingson Pass: the one household that would not leave the forests where its dead lay when its kin went east, and still guides travellers on the wrong side of the mountains.
countries.blazon: A plain field of kingdom green. A beech in full leaf over a low grassed mound in old silver, large in the centre. A silver road winding up to a pass between two hills in moon white, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Aenor Forest

primary_charge.name: a tall fir whose roots spread as wide as its crown
primary_charge.meaning: a stand of the Baelim, one and many, which has never let a man build among it

countries.meaning: The Aenor Forest bears a fir whose roots spread as wide as its crown above a gnarled base: the uncut forest of the Baelim, who have never had a crown, never let a man build among them and never share a forest with the ents.
countries.blazon: A field of dew silver with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of stand green edged by a gnarled line of slow, uneven swellings like old bark. A tall fir whose roots spread as wide as its crown in deep shade, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Cursed Lands

primary_charge.name: a single loose knot in a cord, both ends hanging
primary_charge.meaning: names are knots in a cord: a child is tied into her mother's line and the dead are never untied

countries.meaning: The Cursed Lands bear a cord tied in one knot with its ends hanging free: the Veiled count their years by the ties of the eldest cord and keep every name in its mother's line, and no crown since Aen's has untied them.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, veil grey above and char below, by a cloud-like interlocking line (nebuly), like a cord pulled through loops. A single loose knot in a cord, both ends hanging in undyed wool, large in the centre.

countries.name: Bloody Forest

primary_charge.name: a stag's antlers (attires)
primary_charge.meaning: antler-craft and the forest hunt

secondary_charge.name: a beaded cord hanging
secondary_charge.meaning: kinship by tongue with the Veiled

countries.meaning: The Bloody Forest bears the antlers of the red deer with a beaded cord: the hunting clans of the red-oak forest whose bark bleeds when it is cut, ruled by cord-mothers in peace and by war-chiefs on raids, and never chartered by any king.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, redbark at the hoist and deep bark at the fly, by a cloud-like interlocking line (nebuly), like a cord pulled through loops. A stag's antlers (attires) in antler bone, large in the centre. A beaded cord hanging in ochre, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Lerendor

primary_charge.name: two waves, one above the other
primary_charge.meaning: Lerendor and Veskel under one High Crown

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the ship-crown: a circlet whose points are raised prows

countries.meaning: Lerendor bears two waves under the ship-crown: the High Crown of Lerendor and Veskel, set on one head when Ostrik of the Sonarvik married Runild of Veskel, and the strait dues that make it the North's counterweight to Parim.
countries.blazon: A plain field of strait blue. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in salt white. Two waves, one above the other in salt white, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet whose points are raised ship prows, in salt white.

countries.name: Eekedor

primary_charge.name: a salt cellar
primary_charge.meaning: salt set on the arbitration table binds both parties

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Eekedor bears the salt cellar of its Arbitration Court, where salt shared at the table binds both sides of a quarrel: the council of counting houses that keeps the island's grain and money and holds its court open to any crown that pays.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, salt white above and strait blue below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in deep strait. A salt cellar in deep strait, outlined in salt white, large in the centre.

countries.name: R'en

primary_charge.name: a watch-house on a low cape
primary_charge.meaning: the forts on the strait cape that the first prince of R'en built and refused to pay for

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: R'en bears the watch-house its first prince built on the strait cape and refused to pay for: a gateway principality that has lived between two masters ever since and leans to Parim.
countries.blazon: A field of Leren silver with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of strait blue edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in deep strait. A watch-house on a low cape in deep strait, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Keredor-Hellekton

primary_charge.name: two steering oars joined by one ring
primary_charge.meaning: two coast crowns steered as one

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the ship-crown: a circlet whose points are raised prows

countries.meaning: Keredor-Hellekton impales its two coast crowns and joins their steering oars in one ring, as the Arbitration Court joined Vigda of Keredor and Helmund of Hellekton: a double crown whose court still crowns every heir twice.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, strait blue at the hoist and kelp green at the fly, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in salt white. Two steering oars joined by one ring in clasp gold, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet whose points are raised ship prows, in clasp gold.

countries.name: Molot

primary_charge.name: a crane standing
primary_charge.meaning: the marsh lowlands and a careful watch

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Molot bears the crane that stands watch above the marsh: the margraves whose fortress line behind the marsh took the raiders of the Raiding Years, and who still balance Sonargur against Parim so that neither will ever own them.
countries.blazon: A field of hearth red with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of peat black edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in fleece white. A crane standing in fleece white, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Sensai

primary_charge.name: a bear walking
primary_charge.meaning: the great forest and the oldest crown of the hills

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Sensai's bear wears its crown about its neck: the first and proudest of the North's free crowns, its long vale rich in timber, tar and iron, a partner of the High Crown as long as it is asked rather than told.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, fleece white above and fir green below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. A bear walking in earth brown, outlined in fleece white, large in the centre. The beast wears a small plain crown of fleece white about its neck.

countries.name: Tolhon

primary_charge.name: an otter
primary_charge.meaning: the river-fords and the eel weirs

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Tolhon bears the otter of its fisheries and its herring ban: an island principality of the Onp coast that lives by its toll-bridge at Sirtum and by its distance from everyone else.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper fly corner, fir green above and straw gold below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in fleece white. An otter in peat black, outlined in fleece white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Heodwa Lands

primary_charge.name: a rowan tree in berry
primary_charge.meaning: the rowan planted at every hall door

secondary_charge.name: a war-hammer held upright
secondary_charge.meaning: the Hill Pact, by which the hold comes down to any hill crown that is attacked

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: The Heodwa Lands bear three rowans for the hill crowns of Heodwa, Nuatax and Agniy with the dwarves' hammer of the Hill Pact beneath them: a hill council that every crown of the North knows cannot be fought without fighting Hrakbrund.
countries.blazon: A plain field of fleece white. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. Three of rowan tree in berry, two above one in fir green, large in the centre. A war-hammer held upright in hill grey, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Hrakbrund

primary_charge.name: a squared black gate in a snowline rock face
primary_charge.meaning: the High Gate, the only place where men are received

countries.meaning: Hrakbrund bears its black High Gate on the white peak above Ilmahrim: the dwarves of the High Mountains receive men only at the gate, sell them iron, gold and bombards there, and keep the Hill Pact with the hills below.
countries.blazon: A field of high slate with a reversed pile (a broad wedge rising from the bottom edge to a point near the top) of snow white edged by a dovetailed line of joiner's mortises. A squared black gate in a snowline rock face in gate black, on the reversed pile.

countries.name: Mina

primary_charge.name: a miner's pick
primary_charge.meaning: the hill mines

secondary_charge.name: a mole
secondary_charge.meaning: the miners of the hill, who work unseen

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the gorged crown: the beast wears a small plain crown about its neck, or the crown hangs in the tree's branches

countries.meaning: Mina bears the miner's pick under the crown its king earns by working a season in the Delvings, with the mole of Mine Din, the sister crown joined to it by marriage.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, fleece white above and hill grey below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. A miner's pick in earth brown, outlined in fleece white, large in the centre. A mole in peat black, small, beneath it. A small plain crown of fleece white sits above it.

countries.name: Dolpar

primary_charge.name: a stork
primary_charge.meaning: the nesting storks of the hall roofs (canting on the name)

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Dolpar bears three storks of Stork, one of the walled towns round its deep lake, above the lake-court's green: a lake league of four towns and the market of Parur that settles its own quarrels and competes with Eekedor for the North's.
countries.blazon: A field of straw gold with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of fir green edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in peat black. Three of stork, two above one in earth brown, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Mustnom

primary_charge.name: a laden travel pack
primary_charge.meaning: half of every family always on the road with goods

secondary_charge.name: a pedlar's horn
secondary_charge.meaning: news of a landing carried faster than any courier

marks.text: the boss's iron ring round the charge

countries.meaning: Mustnom bears the laden pack inside the boss's iron ring, with the horn of the packmen who carry news of a landing faster than any courier: boss-warrens whose people are always half on the road.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, pack brown above and road moss below, by a bevilled line with a single sharp offset step. A laden travel pack in trade brass, outlined in boss black, large in the centre. A pedlar's horn in salt white, small, beneath it. Round the charge a plain iron ring of boss black.

countries.name: Coldor

primary_charge.name: a sheaf of winter rye bound with a white cord
primary_charge.meaning: the crown granaries whose bread holds the clans through the long winters

secondary_charge.name: a fire inside a ring of stones
secondary_charge.meaning: the hearth-law: no feud may be carried past a shared fire

marks.text: the winter crown: a white circlet of short icicle points

countries.meaning: Coldor bears the winter rye of its crown granaries under the icicle crown of the Winter Queen, with the clan fire of the clans that swore to her: the strongest crown of the north and the least warlike, whose power is the bread in the Frost-Hall.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, frost white above and winter blue below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A sheaf of winter rye bound with a white cord in hearth red, outlined in frost white, large in the centre. A fire inside a ring of stones in deep night, small, beneath it. Above the charge a circlet of short icicle points in hearth red.

countries.name: Melkgard

primary_charge.name: three spears bound in a sheaf
primary_charge.meaning: the oath-companies that hold the march for the warlord

secondary_charge.name: a storm cloud loosing three bolts
secondary_charge.meaning: the Storm Court, whose captains keep their tokens in the Black Gallery

countries.meaning: Melkgard bears the bound spears of its oath-companies under the storm cloud of the Storm Court: a warlord's march of black forts that took no crown and left none, and whose men would rather go hungry than eat the queen's bread.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, forge black above and war red below, by an indented line of small even teeth. Three spears bound in a sheaf in storm white, large in the centre. A storm cloud loosing three bolts in iron grey, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Horidor

primary_charge.name: a cairn in a mountain gap
primary_charge.meaning: the cairns of the Neridor Gap road, where every western cart pays the cairn-due

secondary_charge.name: a fire inside a ring of stones
secondary_charge.meaning: the hearth-law: no feud may be carried past a shared fire

countries.meaning: Horidor bears the cairn of the Neridor Gap road with Coldor's clan fire beneath it: the cairn moot that keeps the Gap open for every traveller who pays the due and has held the Northern Accord faithfully since the White Year.
countries.blazon: A field of fjord blue with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of snow edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A cairn in a mountain gap in bone, large in the field below the chief. A fire inside a ring of stones in snow, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Yeldenne

primary_charge.name: an arch of two whale ribs
primary_charge.meaning: the bone arches of the halls

secondary_charge.name: a round loaf set on a stone
secondary_charge.meaning: the loaf left each Long Dark at the start of the Silent Road

countries.meaning: Yeldenne bears the whale-rib arch of its valley door and the loaf it leaves each Long Dark at the start of the Silent Road: an ordinary herders' town that pays no tax, asks nothing of the castle above it and gives the traveller supper.
countries.canon_note: Decision L2: an ordinary northern town; never Glo, a green crystal, a knight or a blue sword.
countries.blazon: A plain field of snow. An arch of two whale ribs in soot, large in the centre. A round loaf set on a stone in hide brown, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Fearno

primary_charge.name: a musk ox
primary_charge.meaning: the clan that stands in a ring against the storm

countries.meaning: Fearno's three musk oxen stand together as the herd stands against wolves: the Free Steadings that refused both Fandanar and Minnolomak in 4A 1304 and choose a first lord to speak for them for seven winters.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, ice above and fjord blue below, by an indented line of small even teeth. Three of musk ox, two above one in hide brown, outlined in snow, large in the centre.

countries.name: Austklev

primary_charge.name: a narwhal
primary_charge.meaning: the far ice and its single-tusked whale

countries.meaning: Austklev bears the spear-whale whose tusk it sells south and west: a jarldom of whalers that takes a tithe of every whale brought ashore at Vaestia, keeps the harbour boom and stays out of the Cold Rivalry.
countries.blazon: A plain field of fjord blue. A narwhal in snow, large in the centre.

countries.name: Worlond

primary_charge.name: a turf waystation with a smoking roof
primary_charge.meaning: the forest stages of the Neck Road kept stocked with fodder and dry wood

countries.meaning: Worlond bears the turf waystation of the Neck Road, its roof smoking with dry wood: the forest lordship the Neck Road Compact made to keep the stages stocked for both crowns.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper fly corner, lichen green above and soot below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A turf waystation with a smoking roof in snow, large in the centre.

countries.name: Holdon

primary_charge.name: a tall fair-pole hung with pelts
primary_charge.meaning: the snowline fair at Fentene where men, yeti and goblins trade

marks.text: the tine crown: a circlet of short antler tines

countries.meaning: Holdon bears the fair-pole of Fentene hung with pelts under the tine crown of the king who keeps the snowline fair's peace: a coast kingdom whose kings are judged by one thing, whether the fair was good.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, fjord blue at the hoist and berry red at the fly, by an indented line of small even teeth. A tall fair-pole hung with pelts in bone, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet of short antler tines in bone.

countries.name: Glimkit

primary_charge.name: a round spring sending up three plumes of steam
primary_charge.meaning: Drikzig, the hall of the warm water, dug round the largest spring

secondary_charge.name: a spring snare
secondary_charge.meaning: the best traps of the north

countries.meaning: Glimkit bears the steaming spring of Drikzig with a spring snare beneath it: goblin warrens in the warm valleys of the Coldor Mountains that make the best traps and lamps of the north and pay tax to no crown.
countries.blazon: A field of steam green with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of warren dark edged by a potenty line of T-shaped notches. A round spring sending up three plumes of steam in spring white, large, standing on the base. A spring snare in lamp-fat yellow, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Xison

primary_charge.name: a drop of amber
primary_charge.meaning: the amber traded on the high road

countries.meaning: Xison bears three drops of amber for the upland clans of Xison, Rion and Yeneldmore, who swore a road league at Akahew to keep the high road stretch by stretch and share its tolls.
countries.blazon: A field of hide brown with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of snow edged by an indented line of small even teeth. Three of drop of amber, two above one in amber, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Pertolor

primary_charge.name: a ewe standing
primary_charge.meaning: the one valley of the north where sheep do better than reindeer

countries.meaning: Pertolor bears the ewe of the one valley of the north where sheep do better than reindeer: a wool-market lordship whose lord is cousin to the Winter Queen and godfather to a Melkgard captain, and means to stay both.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, snow above and berry red below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A ewe standing in soot, outlined in snow, large in the centre.

countries.name: Omar

primary_charge.name: a wolverine
primary_charge.meaning: a small clan that yields to nobody

countries.meaning: Omar bears the wolverine that yields to nobody: one clan on one hill-fort above the border moor, owing Coldor for the Hill-Fort Winter and Melkgard for the White Year and paying neither.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, ice above and hide brown below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A wolverine in soot, outlined in snow, large in the centre.

countries.name: Portogalor

primary_charge.name: a walrus
primary_charge.meaning: the ivory coast

countries.meaning: Portogalor bears the walrus whose ivory and fat it sells on the Frozen Sea: sealers descended from the last raider fleet that broke on Melkgard's forts, proud of their forebears and careful not to remind Melkgard of them.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, snow above and soot below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A walrus in bone, outlined in soot, large in the centre.

countries.name: Orewele

primary_charge.name: a rough bloom of iron held in tongs
primary_charge.meaning: the bog-iron and rock-ore of the Orewell lowland

countries.meaning: Orewele bears the bloom of iron it digs from the Orewell lowland and sells by the cartload to the western dwarves: a mining clan whose chief came home a lord from the dwarves' gate and keeps both crowns at arm's length.
countries.blazon: A field of snow with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of hide brown edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A rough bloom of iron held in tongs in fjord blue, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Kvittumm

primary_charge.name: a reindeer's head with full antlers
primary_charge.meaning: the herd, which is the clan's wealth

countries.meaning: Kvittumm bears three antlered heads for the reindeer clans of the white hills, who meet each Long Dark at Esrom and keep the toll-peace with the giants together.
countries.canon_note: Nothing on the arms hints at anything but herds, weather and the winter moot.
countries.blazon: A plain field of white hills. Three of reindeer's head with full antlers, two above one in hide red, large in the centre.

countries.name: Nivaros

primary_charge.name: a throne of ice
primary_charge.meaning: the Ice-Throne of the Frost-King of Nivaros

countries.meaning: Nivaros bears the Ice-Throne of its Frost-King on the arched edge of the glacier: a few thousand giants who let the clans' herds pass for the toll and close their heights to any crown that comes in arms.
countries.blazon: A field of deep ice with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of rime white edged by a single broad arch (enarched). A throne of ice in glacier blue, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Yeti Lands

primary_charge.name: a dark cave mouth in a white peak
primary_charge.meaning: the Hum-Caves where the mountain's hum is answered at dusk

countries.meaning: The Yeti Lands bear the cave that answers the Eldest's song: the shelf clans of Haruhu, who sang the hunting truce at Fentene, divide the seal-grounds with the coast and alone can vouch for an envoy to the heights.
countries.blazon: A field of dusk violet with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of yeti white edged by a dancetty line of three large zigzag peaks. A dark cave mouth in a white peak in yeti white, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Ghaahu

primary_charge.name: a pair of curved wild-herd horns
primary_charge.meaning: the wild herds the height clans follow among the Cold Mountains

countries.meaning: Ghaahu bears the horns of the wild herds its height clans follow among the Cold Mountains, above the three peaks of the yeti line: a land no crown can reach unless a shelf Eldest vouches for its envoy.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, height white above and deep rock below, by a dancetty line of three large zigzag peaks. A pair of curved wild-herd horns in dusk blue, outlined in height white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Vindael

primary_charge.name: a ship under a bellied sail
primary_charge.meaning: ship-shares and the captains' council

countries.meaning: Vindael bears a ship under a bellied sail, owned by shares and sent south since the captains of Porideon first chose a Speaker to hold the harbour book: a council of whalers and sealers on the ice arm that keeps the coast watch.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper fly corner, sea teal above and sail white below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A ship under a bellied sail in tar brown, outlined in sail white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Poloto

primary_charge.name: a bale of furs bound with cord
primary_charge.meaning: the furs the Fandan carries down from the interior to the free port at its mouth

countries.meaning: Poloto bears the bale of furs the Fandan carries down to the free port at its mouth: harbour men who kept Parim's old trading post for themselves, wrote their dues into a harbour book and swear to nobody.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, sail white above and gale blue below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A bale of furs bound with cord in amber, outlined in gale blue, large in the centre.

countries.name: Gunwyn

primary_charge.name: a ring of standing stones
primary_charge.meaning: the Oath-Ring where kings are acclaimed and oaths bind

marks.text: the torc-crown: the king's crown is an open torc

countries.meaning: Gunwyn bears the Oath-Ring of Bulligon under the torc-crown on its two clan colours: a king acclaimed at the stones for life and bound by the Lawspeaker, who signed the Truce of the Grey Ford over the war-thanes' grumbling.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, clan madder at the hoist and clan green at the fly, by an indented line of small even teeth. A ring of standing stones in torc gold, large in the centre. Above the charge an open torc worn as a crown, in torc gold.

countries.name: Werlendor

primary_charge.name: a boar
primary_charge.meaning: the old feud-clans

marks.text: the torc-crown: the king's crown is an open torc

countries.meaning: Werlendor bears the boar of the old feud-clans under a torc-crown of its own: the hill kingdom of Caer-Erg, where Emric had himself acclaimed at the Erg stone, whose kings still call themselves the heirs of Bulligon.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, lime white above and moor brown below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A boar in clan madder, outlined in lime white, large in the centre. Above the charge an open torc worn as a crown, in clan madder.

countries.name: Lambin

primary_charge.name: a round stone granary with a conical roof
primary_charge.meaning: Branorn's granaries below the hills of Faennon, which fed every clan in the famine years

countries.meaning: Lambin bears the round stone granary Branorn built below the hills to feed every clan in the famine years: the West's granary and its neutral ground, where courts that must talk without losing face send their envoys.
countries.blazon: A field of clan green with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of lime white edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A round stone granary with a conical roof in torc gold, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Thenon

primary_charge.name: an olive tree in fruit
primary_charge.meaning: the olives of the West's mildest corner

marks.text: the torc-crown: the king's crown is an open torc

countries.meaning: Thenon bears the olive tree of the West's mildest corner under the torc-crown: a quiet, rich lowland kingdom that bought its peace with cattle and olives and sends its men to the Ronbo Watch.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, slate blue above and torc gold below, by an indented line of small even teeth. An olive tree in fruit in clan green, outlined in lime white, large in the centre. Above the charge an open torc worn as a crown, in lime white.

countries.name: Varnondor

primary_charge.name: a lantern on a cape
primary_charge.meaning: the lanterns King Oslin set on the western capes to watch the old approaches

marks.text: the torc-crown: the king's crown is an open torc

countries.meaning: Varnondor bears the lantern King Oslin first set on the western capes to watch the old approaches, under the torc-crown: the sea watch of the West and its natural staging port for any crossing.
countries.blazon: A plain field of clan green. A lantern on a cape in torc gold, large in the centre. Above the charge an open torc worn as a crown, in torc gold.

countries.name: Girdon

primary_charge.name: three stepping stones
primary_charge.meaning: the ford kept clear by the wardens

countries.meaning: Girdon bears the stepping stones of the ford of Arligon, where the first wardens swore to keep every crossing and judge every quarrel on the river by one law: a commonwealth of wardens, each named for the ford he keeps.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, river green above and water blue below, by an indented line of small even teeth. Three stepping stones in ford stone, large in the centre.

countries.name: Wennarith

primary_charge.name: a ferry raft on its rope
primary_charge.meaning: the ferry-wardens who keep every crossing of the peninsula's rivers

countries.meaning: Wennarith bears the ferry raft on its rope above the river: the ferry-wardens of Datidon and Pernogon, who keep every crossing of the peninsula's rivers on the model of Girdon's fords and are in no hurry to join anyone's war.
countries.blazon: A field of reed gold with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of water blue edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A ferry raft on its rope in dark pool, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Saopon

primary_charge.name: a book bound with a cord
primary_charge.meaning: contracts are sworn on the guild book, not on a god

countries.meaning: Saopon bears the guild book on which the towns of the Kulolo swore their league and stopped paying Parim, on the quartered colours of a guild city: a league that weighs Aenoran gold against Aenoran tariffs every year.
countries.blazon: A field quartered guild green and ivory, the upper hoist quarter {0}, by an indented line of small even teeth. A book bound with a cord in guild wine, outlined in ivory, large over all in the centre.

countries.name: Kradlon

primary_charge.name: a pair of bellows
primary_charge.meaning: the smiths

countries.meaning: Kradlon bears the bellows of the workshops that bought the dwarves' powder secret and make powder-pieces and bombards for anyone who pays: the first guild port of the West, the old settler harbour of Bolbin.
countries.blazon: A field quartered guild wine and ivory, the upper hoist quarter {0}, by an indented line of small even teeth. A pair of bellows in guild gold, outlined in ink black, large over all in the centre.

countries.name: Corogon

primary_charge.name: two wax seals hanging side by side from one cord
primary_charge.meaning: two consuls chosen each year by the great houses, who seal together

countries.meaning: Corogon bears two seals hanging from one cord for the two consuls its great merchant houses choose each year: the consulate of Oslodon, the first Aenoran settlement of the western coast, which fears the corsairs and resents Parim's tariffs.
countries.blazon: A field quartered guild blue and guild gold, the upper hoist quarter {0}, by an indented line of small even teeth. Two wax seals hanging side by side from one cord in vermilion, outlined in ivory, large over all in the centre.

countries.name: Buldor

primary_charge.name: a square company banner on a halberd shaft
primary_charge.meaning: the Banner-Oath: the banner is the company's soul, and a fallen banner ends a company

secondary_charge.name: a sealed roll
secondary_charge.meaning: the contract-book

marks.text: a border compony of livery red and buff: the companies' livery

countries.meaning: Buldor bears the company banner, which is a company's soul, within the livery border of its companies and above the sealed contract-book: a company state at the crossroads of Toples that hires its banners and gunners to the highest bidder.
countries.blazon: A field of steel blue within a border of livery red edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A square company banner on a halberd shaft in buff, large within the border. A sealed roll in olive, small, beneath it. The border is compony: alternating blocks of livery red and buff.

countries.name: Dobbum

primary_charge.name: a basket of round loaves
primary_charge.meaning: the Famine Bread: the grain the small folk carried over the Ronbo passes to starving clansmen, who swore the Ronbo Oath to guard the passes for ever

countries.meaning: Dobbum bears the basket of the Famine Bread above the double-arched hills of its green basin: the small folk who carried grain to starving clansmen and were given the Ronbo Watch in return, so that evil has not entered the basin since.
countries.blazon: A field of basin green with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of hedge dark edged by two low arches side by side. A basket of round loaves in harvest yellow, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Brundahrim

primary_charge.name: a forge-flame on a hearth-stone
primary_charge.meaning: Hrennost, the fire-hold, ruled from its deepest hall

countries.meaning: Brundahrim bears the forge-flame of Hrennost, the fire-hold, under a dovetailed chief of gold: dwarves of the Herlitz and Dusty Mountains who sell gold and powder-pieces at the Outer Gate to whoever wins their favour and keep the small folk's high passes shut.
countries.blazon: A field of hold dark with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of rim gold edged by a dovetailed line of joiner's mortises. A forge-flame on a hearth-stone in forge red, outlined in ash white, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Gromkerm

primary_charge.name: a squared outer gate in a rock face, shut
primary_charge.meaning: the Outer Gate where men trade and beyond which they have never been

secondary_charge.name: a squat bombard on a timber bed
secondary_charge.meaning: the siege bombards cast for sale

countries.meaning: Gromkerm bears the shut Outer Gate above the Kulolo with a bombard beneath it: the old hold of Hrunost, whose gate-wardens sell iron and siege bombards and let no armed company within a bowshot of the gate.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, grey stone above and iron black below, by a dovetailed line of joiner's mortises. A squared outer gate in a rock face, shut in rim gold, outlined in iron black, large in the centre. A squat bombard on a timber bed in ash white, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Goldoroth

primary_charge.name: a fire-mountain with a plume of flame
primary_charge.meaning: the Fire-Mountain above Cocanoor, whose nature the orcs do not speak of

marks.text: the tusk crown: a circlet of upturned tusks

countries.meaning: Goldoroth bears the Fire-Mountain under the tusk crown of the Warking whom the moot of four clan blocs acclaims: the forge-kingdom of Cocanoor that wants the whole Dark Lands, casts bombards with goblin powder and binds its tributaries with the Iron Yoke.
countries.blazon: A plain field of obsidian. A fire-mountain with a plume of flame in lava red, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet of upturned tusks in lava red.

countries.name: Dark Gate

primary_charge.name: a black ridge split by a narrow gap
primary_charge.meaning: the dark gate in the ridge (canting on Dark Gate)

marks.text: the Iron Yoke: a narrow border raguly of ash grey

countries.meaning: The Dark Gate bears the cleft of the only pass from the Goldoroth arm to the south inside the raguly border of the Iron Yoke: a gate-hold that has tolled every caravan since Zugash built his fort at Doldes and pays its tribute to the Warking.
countries.placement: on the lower part of the field
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, ember orange above and ash black below, by a raguly line of lopped-branch stubs. A black ridge split by a narrow gap in sulphur, large on the lower part of the field. A narrow border raguly of ash grey.

countries.name: Dondor

primary_charge.name: a bearded axe
primary_charge.meaning: the clan war and the king chosen from the strongest line

secondary_charge.name: a forged bar with ring ends
secondary_charge.meaning: the bar of iron kept at every hearth and passed to the eldest son

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
the iron band: a plain iron crown with no points

countries.meaning: Dondor bears the bearded axe of its Brute-Kings above the hearth-iron, under the plain iron band: descendants of an Aenoran garrison who took their orc neighbours' insult for a boast and lead the Dark Sea Accord.
countries.blazon: A plain field of hold black. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in bone. A bearded axe in ash, large in the centre. A forged bar with ring ends in bone, small, beneath it. Above the charge a plain iron band without points, in ash.

countries.name: Blackton

primary_charge.name: a high-prowed ship with one square sail
primary_charge.meaning: the fleets of the strait

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Blackton bears three Leren cogs over Dondor's black and the strait's blue: five walled harbour towns of mixed Dondric and Leren blood that sell Dondor's iron to the North, want no king and argue about their charter.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, hold black above and strait blue below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in bone. Three of high-prowed ship with one square sail, two above one in bone, large in the centre.

countries.name: Belonton

primary_charge.name: a cone of salt
primary_charge.meaning: the tithe of salt paid to the sea

countries.meaning: Belonton bears three cones of the Salt Tithe: the sea-orc confederacy sworn at Notle so that its ships would raid others rather than each other, under a Sea-Chief chosen by the voyages he has won.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, salt teal above and tar below, by a raguly line of lopped-branch stubs. Three of cone of salt, two above one in salt white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Bordon

primary_charge.name: a toll bar
primary_charge.meaning: the iron road tolls

countries.meaning: Bordon bears the toll-bar of the Black Road: a hold that turned the barracks of the Buried Wars into caravan inns, takes Volgan's gifts and Goldoroth's threats with the same grin and knows exactly where the Troll Forest begins.
countries.blazon: A field of coal with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of steel edged by a raguly line of lopped-branch stubs. A toll bar in forge orange, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Dreson

primary_charge.name: a bundle of fen reeds
primary_charge.meaning: the reed-council of the fens

countries.meaning: Dreson bears the reeds of the fens where the orcs who would not fight for the Necromancer built a hall on black piles: a fen-hold under a reed-council that lives on eels, peat and bog-iron and swallows the armies that come after it.
countries.blazon: A field of slag green with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of coal edged by a raguly line of lopped-branch stubs. A bundle of fen reeds in steel, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Dulundur

primary_charge.name: four flames rising from one hearth
primary_charge.meaning: the Four Fires lit in one hall at Lesderle

secondary_charge.name: a ring of iron set with nine studs
secondary_charge.meaning: the Free Moot of the holds

countries.meaning: Dulundur bears the four fires lit in one hall at Lesderle, with the ring of the Free Moot it hosts against the Iron Yoke: four valleys that each keep their own chief and their own fire, and burn them together.
countries.form_note: A confederation of four: the four fires are the members, so the charge is not tripled.
countries.blazon: A plain field of rust. Four flames rising from one hearth in steel, large in the centre. A ring of iron set with nine studs in coal, small, beneath it.

countries.name: The Darks

primary_charge.name: a haunch of meat
primary_charge.meaning: the meat Grimduth carried into the ogres' caves instead of spears, which made one moot of orcs and ogres

countries.meaning: The Darks bear the haunch of meat that Grimduth carried into the ogres' caves instead of spears in the hard winter of 4A 1222: one moot of the forest orc holds and the ogre clans at Notdertu.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, coal at the hoist and iron at the fly, by a raguly line of lopped-branch stubs. A haunch of meat in ogre bone, large in the centre.

countries.name: Skragdurg

primary_charge.name: a smoking charcoal clamp
primary_charge.meaning: the charcoal of the Fonoor Forest

countries.meaning: Skragdurg bears the smoking charcoal clamp of the Fonoor Forest: the forest-hold that sells timber and charcoal to every shipwright on the straits, whatever master they serve.
countries.blazon: A field of slag green with a reversed pile (a broad wedge rising from the bottom edge to a point near the top) of steel edged by a raguly line of lopped-branch stubs. A smoking charcoal clamp in coal, on the reversed pile.

countries.name: Britadon

primary_charge.name: a single forge hammer
primary_charge.meaning: the smith-chiefs

countries.meaning: Britadon bears the forge-hammer of the iron hills that Bredesk of the Brakgul made one hold with the headland of Beriath: a hold that sells its iron by sea, sits at the Free Moot and watches Goldoroth's border.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, slag green above and coal below, by a raguly line of lopped-branch stubs. A single forge hammer in steel, large in the centre.

countries.name: Dun

primary_charge.name: a gate hung to swing both ways
primary_charge.meaning: the toll-king who swings to whichever neighbour pays best

marks.text: the toll-king's crown: a circlet hung with small bone charms

countries.meaning: Dun bears a gate hung to swing both ways under the toll-king's crown of bone charms: the crown of the Dun Sea's mouth that swings to whichever neighbour pays best, which has made it the least trusted in the Dark Lands.
countries.blazon: A plain field of hide brown. A gate hung to swing both ways in bone, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet hung with small bone charms, in bone.

countries.name: Wild Lands

primary_charge.name: three casting bones
primary_charge.meaning: the Bone-Casting

countries.meaning: The Wild Lands bear the casting bones that decide whose winter it is: a moor without a council where broken clans go when no hold will have them, held by whoever stays through a winter and contested by everyone else.
countries.blazon: A field of lucky ochre with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of peat edged by a raguly line of lopped-branch stubs. Three casting bones in peat, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Troll Forest

primary_charge.name: a great boulder
primary_charge.meaning: the stone that feeds them

secondary_charge.name: a knotted club
secondary_charge.meaning: the challenge that decides who leads

countries.meaning: The Troll Forest bears the great boulder of its king above the club that smashes camps by night: the forest of the troll king of these trolls only, which leaves alone the realms that pay the troll silver.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, troll moss above and bog black below, by an urdy line of pointed stakes. A great boulder in stone grey, outlined in bog black, large in the centre. A knotted club in bone, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Hoorunoron

primary_charge.name: a cairn of three great stones
primary_charge.meaning: the cairns that name the dead, kept by the oldest giant

marks.text: an orle of iron grey: held inside the land of Dondor

countries.meaning: Hoorunoron bears a cairn of three great stones inside an orle of Dondor's iron grey: a few hundred giants behind the Borderline of Giants who never attack first and carry trespassers back over the cairn-line, one under each arm.
countries.blazon: A field of giant-forest green with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of forest earth edged by a single broad arch (enarched). A cairn of three great stones in lichen white, large, standing on the base. An orle (a narrow inner frame set in from the edges) of iron grey.

countries.name: Burnikit

primary_charge.name: a bulging powder pouch with a smouldering cord
primary_charge.meaning: the best powder of the Dark Lands, sold to whoever pays most

countries.meaning: Burnikit bears the powder pouch of the best powder-makers of the Dark Lands: free warrens under a Big Snik, the loudest and cleverest boss, chosen first to lie to the Necromancer's recruiters and since to sell to whoever pays most.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, rust above and cave black below, by a potenty line of T-shaped notches. A bulging powder pouch with a smouldering cord in hoard gold, large in the centre.

countries.name: Veshazel

primary_charge.name: an ash-grey flame
primary_charge.meaning: the Goldoroth Ash Fields, where ash covers everything and nothing grows

secondary_charge.name: a seal with a blank face
secondary_charge.meaning: the pact-name that only the lord's pact knows

countries.meaning: Veshazel bears an ash-grey flame above a blank seal for the pact-name only its pact knows: a demon lordship on the Goldoroth Ash Fields, sworn to neither Volgan nor Goldoroth, shunned by its neighbours and courted by the Southern Dominion.
countries.blazon: A plain field of ash-hall black. An ash-grey flame in ash grey, large in the centre. A seal with a blank face in ember gold, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Puvulan

primary_charge.name: an arched gate standing open, dark within, with ember light at its threshold
primary_charge.meaning: the Gate of Nafeher and the rite of Names and Gates

secondary_charge.name: a ring of short notches
secondary_charge.meaning: the names the necromantic orders keep

countries.meaning: Puvulan shows the Gate of Nafeher within the ring of names its necromantic orders keep: the Dominion of the dust fields, whose arms show the gate and never the Great Spirit who raised it.
countries.canon_note: Volgan's realm shows the Gate of Nafeher; no figure of Volgan.
countries.blazon: A plain field of grave black. An arched gate standing open, dark within, with ember light at its threshold in bone, large in the centre. A ring of short notches in ember red, encircling it.

countries.name: Mirolon

primary_charge.name: a heron standing on one leg
primary_charge.meaning: the lake-watch: Mirolon's own name

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Mirolon bears the heron that stands watch on one leg by its lake: a free warden-realm whose High Warden is chosen for life, whose beacon towers are manned every night, and which alone takes the signs from the south seriously.
countries.blazon: A plain field of night blue. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in heron white. A heron standing on one leg in heron white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Khorvrath

primary_charge.name: a single curved horn
primary_charge.meaning: the pact-horn of a lord of the Nether

marks.text: a narrow base of grave black: the realm stands on the Dominion's ground

countries.meaning: Khorvrath bears the pact-horn of the horn-hold of Khorvazel on the grave-black ground of the Dominion: the horned court of the Southern Dominion, which keeps its oath to Nafeher while Volgan's strength stands and still demands the thralls who fled to Olen.
countries.blazon: A field of ash black with a pile (a broad wedge from the top edge narrowing to a point near the bottom) of nether red edged by a rent line, jagged like torn hide. A single curved horn in ember gold, on the pile. A narrow plain base of grave black.

countries.name: Dolon

primary_charge.name: a cauldron of brine over fire
primary_charge.meaning: salt and sulphur made into black powder

marks.text: a narrow base of grave black: the realm stands on the Dominion's ground

countries.meaning: Dolon bears the brine cauldron over the fire where the salt of its coast and the sulphur of the Maw make the Dominion's black powder: the forge of the Southern Dominion, whose laws are written in salt so that the sea can wash away any oath its queen regrets.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, obsidian above and nether red below, by a rent line, jagged like torn hide. A cauldron of brine over fire in ember gold, large in the centre. A narrow plain base of grave black.

countries.name: Nezer

primary_charge.name: a galley on a wave of fire
primary_charge.meaning: the galleys that cross the Sea of Lava, which only demons sail

marks.text: a narrow base of grave black: the realm stands on the Dominion's ground

countries.meaning: Nezer bears the galley that crosses the Sea of Lava to the Nether on a field divided between its two crowns of one family, standing on the Dominion's grave-black ground: the largest of the sworn realms and the keeper of the broken Burning Gate on its coast.
countries.form_note: A confederacy of two crowns: the field is divided between them instead of tripling the charge.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, nether red above and ash black below, by a rent line, jagged like torn hide. A galley on a wave of fire in ash white, large in the centre. A narrow plain base of grave black.

countries.name: Nether

primary_charge.name: a five-pointed figure drawn in one unbroken line inside a ring of flame
primary_charge.meaning: the King of Demons' seal over the pacts of every house

marks.text: the hall-crown: a circlet of flame-points

countries.meaning: The Nether bears the King of Demons' seal, a five-pointed figure drawn in one unbroken line inside a ring of fire, under the hall-crown: the court beneath the volcanic island whose pacts bind every house and which sells companies to Nafeher only by bargain.
countries.canon_note: The pentagram is allowed in a demon sigil (owner, 24 October 2026); the King's name is never shown.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, hall black above and lava red below, by a rent line, jagged like torn hide. A five-pointed figure drawn in one unbroken line inside a ring of flame in pact gold, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet of flame-points in pact gold.

countries.name: Halia

primary_charge.name: a salt-pan with heaped salt
primary_charge.meaning: the salt trade and the salt laid in every grave

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Halia bears three salt-pans for the freeholds of the salt coast that swore at Halon to pay one toll as one league, so that no freehold could be squeezed alone: salt-makers who pay Nafeher for silence and remember the thief only in their taverns.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, sand above and sea teal below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in tar black. Three of salt-pan with heaped salt, two above one in tar black, large in the centre.

countries.name: Nan

primary_charge.name: a gaff hook
primary_charge.meaning: the warlord who takes the tolls

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief

countries.meaning: Nan bears the gaff hook of the warlord who takes its tolls: the realm of the strongest captain of the Nan Mountains, who lends the Dominion its storm-pilots and sells the same pilots to anyone who pays more.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, tar black above and sand below, by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in salt white. A gaff hook in salt white, outlined in tar black, large in the centre.

countries.name: Olen

primary_charge.name: a storm lantern
primary_charge.meaning: a light kept against the storms (canting on Luminor and the lamp-cliffs of Olen)

countries.meaning: Olen bears the lantern that the Holy Breeze kept lit on its cliffs for a whole winter: a shrine-realm of lamp-keepers whose lights are the first a ship sees coming out of the storm belt, and who shelter whoever reaches them.
countries.blazon: A field of salt white with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of storm grey edged by a straight line. A storm lantern in tar black, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Zol's Mistake

primary_charge.name: a sigil of broken concentric rings
primary_charge.meaning: The Will of Zol, the emblem that leads the realm; nothing about who governs for Zol is said

countries.meaning: Zol's Mistake shows only the sigil of its emblem leader, the Will of Zol: broken concentric rings on the void, which say nothing of who administers Furviatlon.
countries.canon_note: Emblem realm: the Will of Zol alone; nothing of Zol, of his servant or of the black isles appears.
countries.blazon: A plain field of void black. A sigil of broken concentric rings in cold grey, large in the centre.

countries.name: Worshipdom

primary_charge.name: a hand from the base offering a round loaf
primary_charge.meaning: the loaf given to the stranger; the hand is unarmed and gives

secondary_charge.name: a pilgrim's staff
secondary_charge.meaning: the pilgrims of the Zilin valleys

countries.meaning: The Worshipdom shows only its public charity: a hand offering a loaf above the pilgrim's staff, the hostels of the Deliverer that shelter pilgrims from every land and carry letters for every court.
countries.canon_note: Public arms of a secret realm: nothing may reveal Afrit or the Hidden Council (deny-list of 1.5), and no lamp with an open flame (the arms of Lumae of the twelve).
countries.blazon: A plain field of hostel white. A hand from the base offering a round loaf in bread brown, large in the centre. A pilgrim's staff in bread brown, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Magical Forest

primary_charge.name: a green-leaved tree with its roots
primary_charge.meaning: the cities woven into living trees

secondary_charge.name: a book of precedents bound in green
secondary_charge.meaning: the council's book renewed each century

marks.text: a border engrailed: the elected speakers

countries.meaning: The Magical Forest bears the tree of the Singing Grove, which its houses say was sung before it grew, above the book of precedents its elected council keeps, inside the silver border of elected speakers: the oldest realm of the elves, never conquered and the keeper of the Refusal.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, leaf green above and deep wood below, by an engrailed line of small inward scallops. A green-leaved tree with its roots in elven silver, large in the centre. A book of precedents bound in green in moon white, small, beneath it. A narrow border engrailed of elven silver.

countries.name: Herrodon

primary_charge.name: a long stair cut into a hillside
primary_charge.meaning: halls cut into hillsides

secondary_charge.name: a silver road winding up to a pass between two hills
secondary_charge.meaning: the road to the Kingson Pass that the household guides travellers on

marks.text: the leaf circlet: a silver circlet of upright leaves

countries.meaning: Herrodon bears the stair of the hall where each queen is acclaimed by the houses of the hills, under the leaf circlet, with the road west to the lost kin it still remembers: a hill queenship that keeps the Boundary Groves feud with Andos Enda alive by ceremony.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, hill green above and night slate below, by an engrailed line of small inward scallops. A long stair cut into a hillside in elven silver, large in the centre. A silver road winding up to a pass between two hills in scale gold, small, beneath it. Above the charge a circlet of upright leaves in elven silver.

countries.name: Andos Enda

primary_charge.name: a boat with a glass canopy
primary_charge.meaning: the boat-houses with glass roofs

countries.meaning: Andos Enda bears three glass boats for the lake groves that swore the Weir Compact to share the water: a federation whose boats carry the letters between Sonargur and the elven realms and whose Water-Court judges at the weir.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, lake teal above and deep blue below, by an engrailed line of small inward scallops. Three of boat with a glass canopy, two above one in water silver, large in the centre.

countries.name: Nolorim

primary_charge.name: two peaks with a path between them
primary_charge.meaning: the Nolorim Passes
