countries.meaning: Nolorim bears the pass under the snow that its families have kept for centuries, each counting every pilgrim, merchant and stranger who crosses: the pass-wardenship sworn when Volgan's fires burned below the Nolorim East Pass, each family to one post, so that nothing of his would come up through the heights.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, snow white above and pass grey-green below, by an engrailed line of small inward scallops. Two peaks with a path between them in pine, outlined in snow white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Lccimio

primary_charge.name: a slender shore tower with a lantern roof
primary_charge.meaning: the house-towers of the shore

marks.text: a border engrailed: the elected speakers

countries.meaning: Lccimio bears the lantern tower of its rift-coast quays inside the silver border of its council of elder houses: the elves who know the eastern courts better than any alive, and who will be the first to meet an eastern landing.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, rift teal above and night sea below, by an engrailed line of small inward scallops. A slender shore tower with a lantern roof in quay silver, large in the centre. A narrow border engrailed of quay silver.

countries.name: Eldafaen

primary_charge.name: a rolled scroll tied with a silver cord
primary_charge.meaning: the Archive: the names, letters and songs of the elves who died in the Alliance's wars

countries.meaning: Eldafaen bears the tied scroll of the Archive, where a house of loremasters keeps the names, letters and songs of the elves who died in the Alliance's wars so that no one will again ask the elves to march without reading them first.
countries.blazon: A plain field of night sea. A rolled scroll tied with a silver cord in quay silver, large in the centre.

countries.name: Yavieth

primary_charge.name: a mountain with three spurs
primary_charge.meaning: Dragon Mountain, on whose three spurs the dragons roost

secondary_charge.name: a single shed dragon scale
secondary_charge.meaning: the scales the dragons shed, which the keepers trade at Kingson

countries.meaning: Yavieth bears the three spurs of Dragon Mountain with a shed dragon scale beneath them: a fellowship without a ruler whose roost-keepers go up to the roosts to listen rather than to command, and trade the shed scales at Kingson.
countries.blazon: A plain field of keeper silver. A mountain with three spurs in roost slate, large in the centre. A single shed dragon scale in dragon red, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Teste

primary_charge.name: a ploughed furrow running across the field
primary_charge.meaning: the one fertile vale under the Herrodon rim, ploughed by the descendants of the Third Age refugees

marks.text: Aen's label of three points in chief
Herrodon's ward: a narrow border engrailed of night slate

countries.meaning: Teste bears the ploughed furrow of the one fertile vale under the Herrodon rim, within the border of the hall that protects it: a commune of men descended from Third Age refugees, who feed Herrodon and Andos Enda and choose their Reeve at the harvest moot.
countries.blazon: A field of vale green with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of straw edged by a straight line. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in loam brown. A ploughed furrow running across the field in linen white, large in the field below the chief. A narrow border engrailed of night slate.

countries.name: Luv-zhise

primary_charge.name: a flat ferry-boat with a square sail
primary_charge.meaning: the ferries the Alerhic boatmen ran across the Rift Narrows for centuries

countries.meaning: Luv-zhise bears the ferry crossing between the two shores of the Rift Narrows, its far shore in the silver of the elves who chartered the quay-houses: a free port that lives on the crossing to the East and sides with whoever holds it.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, narrows teal at the hoist and quay silver at the fly, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A flat ferry-boat with a square sail in ferry plum, outlined in foam white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Mushroom Forest

primary_charge.name: a ring of pale mushroom caps
primary_charge.meaning: the fungal belt of the rift shore

marks.text: an orle of rift teal: held inside the land of Lccimio

countries.meaning: The Mushroom Forest bears a ring of pale mushroom caps inside an orle of the rift coast's teal: the land of the mycids along the rift shore, a people that trades through Luv-zhise and whose ways of rule nobody outside the forest knows.
countries.canon_note: Proposed until the owner rules on the mycids: nothing about their rule is drawn.
countries.blazon: A plain field of spore purple. A ring of pale mushroom caps in cap cream, large in the centre. An orle (a narrow inner frame set in from the edges) of rift teal.

countries.name: Gala

primary_charge.name: a round pool rimmed in gold, with rain falling into it
primary_charge.meaning: the Mirror of First Rain: the past and the possible glimpsed, and never trusted plainly

marks.text: the endless circlet: a plain gold circlet with no points

countries.meaning: Gala bears the Mirror of First Rain under the endless circlet of King Lorien, above the green shore its Sunfolk villages farm: the oldest elven court of Aoaz, courteous to Aenor and distrustful of kings who turn victories into crowns.
countries.blazon: A field of court white with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of shade green edged by an invected line of small outward scallops. A round pool rimmed in gold, with rain falling into it in rain blue, outlined in deep harbour, large, standing on the base. Above the charge a plain circlet with no points, in deep harbour.

countries.name: The Lands of Light

primary_charge.name: a tall arched doorway with a sun disc resting in its arch
primary_charge.meaning: the sanctuary threshold where the light of the Sea of Gods is received

countries.meaning: The Lands of Light bear the noon-door that only they may bear: the sanctuaries of the eastern lowland that chose one Radiant Speaker to share out the water of Sun Lake in the drought of 1A 840, and that still chair the Noon Council.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, sanctuary white above and noon gold below, by a rayonny line of alternating straight and flame-shaped rays. A tall arched doorway with a sun disc resting in its arch in flame orange, large in the centre.

countries.name: Elvana

primary_charge.name: a tall spindle wound with a skein
primary_charge.meaning: the weavers of the Cape of Elvana

countries.meaning: Elvana bears the spindle of the weavers of its cape sanctuary: a small, gentle house of weavers and healers that chose its own Speaker rather than answer to Eldoga and keeps its one quarrel in the world with Igara.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, sanctuary white above and shade blue below, by a rayonny line of alternating straight and flame-shaped rays. A tall spindle wound with a skein in deep red, outlined in sanctuary white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Igara

primary_charge.name: a crane wading
primary_charge.meaning: the shrine of the shallows on Sun Lake and its cranes

countries.meaning: Igara bears the crane of its shrine of the shallows on Sun Lake: the smallest sanctuary realm, which chose its own Speaker sixty-two years after Elvana and measures its standing at the Noon Council by how often it can outvote it.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, sanctuary gold at the hoist and sanctuary white at the fly, by a rayonny line of alternating straight and flame-shaped rays. A crane wading in shade blue, large in the centre.

countries.name: Yeni Alang

primary_charge.name: a pair of wings seen from below
primary_charge.meaning: the wings seen over the terraces on a still day, kept in the Roll of Wings

countries.meaning: Yeni Alang bears a pair of wings seen from below on its rising terrace: the house of sky-watchers founded when one of them saw wings over the terraces on a still day, which still adds a line to the Roll of Wings a few times in a good year.
countries.blazon: A field of sanctuary white with a reversed pile (a broad wedge rising from the bottom edge to a point near the top) of shade blue edged by a rayonny line of alternating straight and flame-shaped rays. A pair of wings seen from below in sanctuary white, on the reversed pile.

countries.name: Tor Luni

primary_charge.name: three standing stones of uneven height
primary_charge.meaning: the standing stones older than any Sunhot record, kept uncut among the quarries

countries.meaning: Tor Luni bears three standing stones of uneven height, older than any Sunhot record and kept uncut among the quarries: the sanctuary of the Keeper of the Stones, whose white stone builds half the realms of the region.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, sanctuary gold above and deep red below, by a rayonny line of alternating straight and flame-shaped rays. Three standing stones of uneven height in sanctuary white, outlined in deep red, large in the centre.

countries.name: Ihuy

primary_charge.name: an island peak trailing smoke
primary_charge.meaning: Hol, whose Great Volcano threw ash over every island at once

countries.meaning: Ihuy bears Hol, the isle whose Great Volcano threw ash over every island at once and made one council of the seven isle Speakers: a council of sailors, pearl-farmers and fishers that watches the smoke of Hol.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, isle gold above and isle teal below, by a rayonny line of alternating straight and flame-shaped rays. An island peak trailing smoke in deep lagoon, large in the centre.

countries.name: Soyano

primary_charge.name: a tall white ship
primary_charge.meaning: the white ships of the south and the hulls of Gala's court

countries.meaning: Soyano bears the white ship of its shipwrights: the Archipelago Council of the northern isles under a Tide-Speaker chosen at the turn of the tide, which builds the white ships of the south and the hulls of Gala's court.
countries.blazon: A plain field of isle teal. A tall white ship in terrace white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Goodin

primary_charge.name: a broad-crowned shade tree
primary_charge.meaning: guest-towns under shade trees

marks.text: a chief rayonny: the Sunhot patrons

countries.meaning: Goodin bears the shade tree of its guest-towns under the rayonny chief of its Sunhot patrons: Sunfolk steadings that govern themselves under elders, raise levies freely and are the strongest arm of the Noon Council, where they sit as guests.
countries.blazon: A plain field of shade green. A broad-crowned shade tree in linen, large in the centre. A chief rayonny of sun yellow.

countries.name: God Forest

primary_charge.name: a closed gate of woven branches
primary_charge.meaning: the wood the Keepers close to everyone

countries.meaning: The God Forest bears a closed gate of woven branches: the household of Keepers who were there when the first sanctuary was built, who close their wood to everyone and say nothing at all.
countries.canon_note: No sun and no Sunhot or Gala line: the Keepers' kin is open.
countries.blazon: A field of god-wood green with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of shadow edged by a wattled line woven over and under like a hurdle of branches. A closed gate of woven branches in glade gold, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Noris

primary_charge.name: a well-head with rope and bucket
primary_charge.meaning: a well is a promise from the earth; the king is chosen by the well-lords

secondary_charge.name: a camel kneeling
secondary_charge.meaning: the guest's camel kneels at the well

marks.text: the well-crown: a silver circlet set with small cups

countries.meaning: Noris bears the well of the Seven Wells of Furvior under the well-crown of the king the well-lords choose from one line, with the kneeling camel of the tribes he leads in war: the camel-kingship of the northern desert and the Salt Road.
countries.canon_note: The one camel of the East (the Moco tribes are now part of Noris).
countries.blazon: A plain field of indigo. A well-head with rope and bucket in well ochre, large in the centre. A camel kneeling in robe white, small, beneath it. Above the charge a circlet set with small cups, in well ochre.

countries.name: Naamis

primary_charge.name: two harbour moles curving round one basin
primary_charge.meaning: Hacsen and Vigodor, the two harbours one marriage made a crown

marks.text: the sea-crown: a gold circlet of small wave-crest points

countries.meaning: Naamis bears the two harbour moles of Hacsen and Vigodor that one marriage joined under the sea-crown: a sea crown whose ships carry the Salt Road's goods to the rift and whose policy rests on the Noris Treaty.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, coast white above and naam blue below, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). Two harbour moles curving round one basin in sail ochre, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet of small wave-crest points in sail ochre.

countries.name: Woqood

primary_charge.name: a harpoon with its coiled line
primary_charge.meaning: the Harpoon-Speaker who holds the peace of the moot of Pehami

countries.meaning: Woqood bears three harpoons for the boat clans that swore the moot of Pehami to share the seal grounds without blood under a Harpoon-Speaker: sealers of the snow coast who stay out of every eastern coalition unless someone attacks them.
countries.blazon: A field of seal water with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of snow coast edged by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). Three of harpoon with its coiled line, two above one in snow coast, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Orato

primary_charge.name: a cod swimming
primary_charge.meaning: the catch the isles sell to the Naamis ship-masters

countries.meaning: Orato impales its two isles of Orato and Fladev, joined by marriage, with the cod its families sell to the Naamis ship-masters: a lordship of the boats facing the Kusmeel under one lord who built the stone harbour at Nodoqood.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, isle blue at the hoist and boat brown at the fly, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A cod swimming in net white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Stabilo

primary_charge.name: a balance
primary_charge.meaning: an honest weight pleases the New Gods; a false weight is the worst crime

countries.meaning: Stabilo bears the honest balance of its Prince of the Scales, first of the bench of houses that built the Gold Road from the bronze mines to the sea: the strongest military purse of the East and Noris's rival on the caravan roads.
countries.blazon: A plain field of caravan red. A balance in linen, large in the centre.

countries.name: Drak

primary_charge.name: a smoking mountain cone
primary_charge.meaning: the Drak Furnace, under which the forge-houses swore the Furnace Oath

secondary_charge.name: a bound powder cask
secondary_charge.meaning: the black powder the East learned at Drak

countries.meaning: Drak bears the smoking cone of the Drak Furnace under which its forge-houses swore the Furnace Oath, with the powder cask whose recipe its forge-masters guard: the place where the East learned black powder.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, bronze above and caravan red below, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A smoking mountain cone in ink, outlined in linen, large in the centre. A bound powder cask in linen, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Mostok

primary_charge.name: nested cup-weights
primary_charge.meaning: the weighing halls

countries.meaning: Mostok bears the nested weights of the weighers who built the caravanserai of Cereosa to settle the caravans' quarrels: a junction city of inns and weigh-houses that knows its freedom lasts exactly as long as Noris and Stabilo distrust each other.
countries.blazon: A field of market green with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of bronze edged by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). Nested cup-weights in linen, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Azano

primary_charge.name: a bronze coin stamped with a balance
primary_charge.meaning: the Pact's coinage

countries.meaning: Azano bears the struck coin with which its house bought the charter of Ceralon outright: a city that takes its master's name, independent by charter rather than by arms, whose ledgers record loans to half the courts of the East.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, linen above and market green below, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A bronze coin stamped with a balance in bronze, outlined in linen, large in the centre.

countries.name: Obmi

primary_charge.name: a tall hardwood trunk with a tapping cup
primary_charge.meaning: the hardwood and the jungle gum that seals casks and ships' seams

countries.meaning: Obmi bears the hardwood trunk tapped for the jungle gum that seals casks and ships' seams: the factors' city at the edge of the Obmi Jungle, which lives by the Stabilo Pact's need for casks and fears the jungle's fevers more than any army.
countries.blazon: A field of colonnade stone with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of market green edged by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A tall hardwood trunk with a tapping cup in seal wax, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Pornivior

primary_charge.name: a heaped tithe-bowl held up
primary_charge.meaning: the fire-tithe paid every year without fail

countries.meaning: Pornivior bears the heaped tithe-bowl of the fire-tithe it pays the mountain every year without fail: the waystation city of Nerhuus below Mount Ergo, whose people say a devil once took a whole caravan and left only the scales.
countries.blazon: A field quartered bronze and ink, the upper hoist quarter {0}, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A heaped tithe-bowl held up in linen, large over all in the centre.

countries.name: Alerhia

primary_charge.name: a temple stair of seven steps
primary_charge.meaning: the tall temples above the flood-line

marks.text: the river-diadem: a gold collar-crown worn low
a narrow wavy bendlet: the king's river

countries.meaning: Alerhia bears the stair-temple raised above the flood-line so that the River and the Kings Below would each have a place, under the river-diadem and over the river's band: an old crown in its own right at the end of the Gold Road, rich in grain and scribes.
countries.blazon: A plain field of river gold. A temple stair of seven steps in lapis, large in the centre. Above the charge a low collar-crown in lapis. Behind the charge a narrow wavy diagonal band of lapis.

countries.name: Erco

primary_charge.name: two mountains with a bar across the pass between them
primary_charge.meaning: the passes the mine-lords shut against Volgan's beaten soldiers in 2A 12

marks.text: the river-diadem: a gold collar-crown worn low
a narrow wavy bendlet: the king's river

countries.meaning: Erco bears the barred pass between two mountains that its mine-lords shut in 2A 12 against Volgan's beaten soldiers, under the river-diadem: a mountain kingdom of rich mines and seven manned forts that pays the fire-tithe to the mountain every spring.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, lapis above and linen white below, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). Two mountains with a bar across the pass between them in river gold, outlined in lapis, large in the centre. Above the charge a low collar-crown in river gold. Behind the charge a narrow wavy diagonal band of flood silt.

countries.name: Plutondo

primary_charge.name: a sheaf of grain grown from black ash
primary_charge.meaning: the ash-grown grain of the Plutondo Vents

marks.text: a narrow wavy bendlet: the king's river

countries.meaning: Plutondo bears the sheaf of grain grown in the ash of the Plutondo Vents: a princedom of the warm southern valley, rich in ash-grown grain and ore and deep in Stabilo's ledgers since the Vent Year.
countries.blazon: A field of flood silt with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of river blue edged by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A sheaf of grain grown from black ash in linen white, large, standing on the base. Behind the charge a narrow wavy diagonal band of linen white.

countries.name: Delbiz

primary_charge.name: a horse standing
primary_charge.meaning: the war-horses and the great horse-fair of Furtonlin

marks.text: the river-diadem: a gold collar-crown worn low
a narrow wavy bendlet: the king's river

countries.meaning: Delbiz bears a horse of the great fair at Furtonlin under the river-diadem: the grassland kingdom whose horse-lords swore to keep their horses and their grass for themselves when Alerhia could no longer pay them.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, river gold above and reed green below, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A horse standing in linen white, outlined in lapis, large in the centre. Above the charge a low collar-crown in lapis. Behind the charge a narrow wavy diagonal band of lapis.

countries.name: Ostoroth

primary_charge.name: a lantern on a pole
primary_charge.meaning: the lantern quays of the Lake Road

marks.text: the lantern-crown: a silver circlet of small lantern points

countries.meaning: Ostoroth bears the lantern of the shrine on the water at Ohitus under the lantern-crown, because the highland lords made the lord of Ohitus king so that the shrine would always be in a king's keeping: the kingdom of the Lake Road that keeps the Lantern Peace with Mora.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, deep water above and lake silver-blue below, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A lantern on a pole in lantern amber, outlined in deep water, large in the centre. Above the charge a circlet of small lantern points in lantern amber.

countries.name: Mora

primary_charge.name: a basket heaped with grain
primary_charge.meaning: the three years of harvests that bought the towns' rights, and the granary of the East

secondary_charge.name: a perch
secondary_charge.meaning: the lake's common fish

countries.meaning: Mora bears the basket of harvests with which the fishers and farmers of Gonnois bought their lord's rights, and the perch of the fish-hall where their council meets: the granary of the East, which has no king and wants none.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, quay white above and lake silver-blue below, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A basket heaped with grain in lantern amber, outlined in deep water, large in the centre. A perch in deep water, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Kersian

primary_charge.name: a market gate
primary_charge.meaning: the walled market where the Lake Road crosses the Gold Road

countries.meaning: Kersian bears the gate of the walled market that Aenoran exiles and Alerhic lake traders built where the Lake Road would cross the Gold Road: a free city, rich, small and anxious, kept free by the rivalry of two powers.
countries.blazon: A plain field of lake silver-blue. A market gate in quay white, large in the centre.

countries.name: Rhachia

primary_charge.name: a domed kiln with fire at its mouth
primary_charge.meaning: the kiln-shrines and the Refiring each spring

secondary_charge.name: a clay jar
secondary_charge.meaning: the pots and grain the neighbours borrow

countries.meaning: Rhachia bears the kiln of the kiln-mothers who opened the gates of Pordoce in 4A 1719 and elected a tribune instead of a king, with a jar of the pots the caravan houses still buy: a poor, proud commonwealth watched by the deposed king's heir.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, kiln ochre above and red clay below, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A domed kiln with fire at its mouth in umber, outlined in slip white, large in the centre. A clay jar in slip white, small, beneath it.

countries.name: Miaed

primary_charge.name: a fire burning in a mountain pass
primary_charge.meaning: the fires the pass-lords keep for the spirits of the high road, who lead caravans through the sand-storms

countries.meaning: Miaed bears the fire the pass-lords keep in the Hardtmuth passes for the spirits of the high road: a lordship of pass-forts that elects the Lord of Erdozan and sells passage to Noris and Stabilo alike.
countries.placement: on the lower part of the field
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, sand white above and gorge red below, by a stepped line like a short stair (grady). A fire burning in a mountain pass in fire gold, large on the lower part of the field.

countries.name: Wahatud

primary_charge.name: four well-heads set in a ring
primary_charge.meaning: the four strings of wells round Biir-Raab, kept by the Well-Moot

countries.meaning: Wahatud bears the four wells of the Well-Moot that the surviving clan-mothers swore at Biir-Raab after the war of the poisoned wells: a league that never joins a war and always offers water to refugees.
countries.form_note: A league of four strings of wells: the four wells are the members, so the charge is not tripled.
countries.blazon: A plain field of oasis green. Four well-heads set in a ring in dune, large in the centre.

countries.name: Enhis Is Rond

primary_charge.name: a stone cairn on a reef
primary_charge.meaning: the reef-shrines

countries.meaning: Enhis Is Rond bears the shrine beneath the tide that the Rising Tide drowned, whose Priest-Elders rule the centre of the Great Isle and repeat in its rites a name they do not understand.
countries.blazon: A plain field of coral sand. A stone cairn on a reef in deep reef, large in the centre.

countries.name: Howan

primary_charge.name: a long house on stilts with its door open
primary_charge.meaning: the house kept for the shipwrecked

countries.meaning: Howan bears the house on stilts kept open for the shipwrecked: a harbour moot of terrace-heads on the River Tich, the only river of note in the islands, whose divers sell pearls for iron.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, coral sand above and lagoon turquoise below, by a wavy line (undy). A long house on stilts with its door open in coral red, outlined in coral sand, large in the centre.

countries.name: Verde

primary_charge.name: a woven sail
primary_charge.meaning: the woven sails of the island boats

countries.meaning: Verde bears the woven sail of the canoes cut from its western hills and mangroves: a clan hall of timber-folk and navigators who sell hull-timber to Aenor Isle and pilots to anyone.
countries.blazon: A field of coral sand with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of frond green edged by a wavy line (undy). A woven sail in lava black, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Nara

primary_charge.name: a woven fish trap
primary_charge.meaning: the reef fishing

countries.meaning: Nara bears the fish trap its villages lift only by day: an elders' moot of fishers on the long island Ancha who will not cross the Night Reef after dark for anyone.
countries.blazon: A field of deep reef with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of coral sand edged by a wavy line (undy). A woven fish trap in coral sand, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Yongyong

primary_charge.name: a shell necklace
primary_charge.meaning: the necklaces of the feasts

countries.meaning: Yongyong bears a necklace of the shell its villages carve: the ring-council of the villages round the Yong lagoon, which all carry one name and burned three of their own in the Year of the Red Wind before they made peace round one ring.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, coral sand above and deep reef below, by a wavy line (undy). A shell necklace in coral red, outlined in coral sand, large in the centre.

countries.name: Kamu Lamo

primary_charge.name: a notched tally stick
primary_charge.meaning: each island counts its dead as waves on the reef

countries.meaning: Kamu Lamo bears the tally itself: the deep isle of the oldest tally-caves of the south, where the dead have been counted as waves on the cave walls since before any Aenoran sailor saw the arcs.
countries.blazon: A plain field of deep reef. A notched tally stick in coral sand, large in the centre.

countries.name: Kea

primary_charge.name: three stepped rice terraces
primary_charge.meaning: the rice that grows on every slope that will hold it

countries.meaning: Kea bears three stepped rice terraces on the rising slope: the terrace council of Kea, Agla and the Rice Islands, which shares its scarce water by council and sends rice to any island in a bad year.
countries.blazon: A field of lagoon turquoise with a reversed pile (a broad wedge rising from the bottom edge to a point near the top) of coral sand edged by a wavy line (undy). Three stepped rice terraces in frond green, on the reversed pile.

countries.name: Sidea

primary_charge.name: a tall slit drum
primary_charge.meaning: the drummers who carry the first warning of every storm

countries.meaning: Sidea bears the slit drum on which its drummers carry the first warning of every storm to the Great Isle: a cluster of islets that chose one elder in the storm year that cut them off for a whole season.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, lagoon turquoise at the hoist and deep reef at the fly, by a wavy line (undy). A tall slit drum in coral sand, large in the centre.

countries.name: Adel

primary_charge.name: a rolled chart
primary_charge.meaning: the chart-house archives

countries.meaning: Adel bears three rolled charts for the chart-houses that agreed in 4A 388 to copy every chart in one house at Sanderz: the chart-house league whose Chart Hall decides which crown gets the newest chart.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, chart paper above and chart teal below, by an indented line of small even teeth. Three of rolled chart, two above one in ink, large in the centre.

countries.name: Raerby

primary_charge.name: a buoy
primary_charge.meaning: the marked channels

countries.meaning: Raerby bears the buoy that marks the banks it mediates: the broker-captains of Ese, who grew rich lending ships and settling others' quarrels for a fee and who watch Nondondor's fleet more closely than anyone.
countries.blazon: A field of ink with a chief (a band across the top, two sevenths of the height) of chart paper edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A buoy in reef coral, large in the field below the chief.

countries.name: Pollos

primary_charge.name: a great strong-room key
primary_charge.meaning: the strong-room where the chart-houses keep their treasury

countries.meaning: Pollos bears the key of the strong-room where the chart-houses keep their treasury: the market isle of Havnai, whose guild-masters wrote the market law every buyer and seller swears to, and who sell everything to everyone.
countries.blazon: A plain field of chart teal. A great strong-room key in sand gold, large in the centre.

countries.name: Fineger

primary_charge.name: a pilot's lantern
primary_charge.meaning: the harbour pilots

countries.meaning: Fineger bears the pilot's lantern of the cold northern isles, whose pilots know waters only they can read: kelp-farmers and shepherds through whom any fleet bound north must pass.
countries.blazon: A field of chart paper with a base (a band across the bottom, two sevenths of the height) of reef coral edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A pilot's lantern in ink, large, standing on the base.

countries.name: Halenor

primary_charge.name: a fire on a shore rock
primary_charge.meaning: the shore-fires the wreck-lord may light or leave dark

countries.meaning: Halenor bears the fire on the shore rock that its wreck-lord chooses each gale season to light or leave dark: the storm isles of the outer south, where the chiefs swore in 3A 280 that whatever the storm brings to a shore belongs to its lord.
countries.blazon: A field of chart teal with a reversed pile (a broad wedge rising from the bottom edge to a point near the top) of sand gold edged by an indented line of small even teeth. A fire on a shore rock in reef coral, on the reversed pile.

countries.name: Seite Islands

primary_charge.name: a turtle
primary_charge.meaning: the turtle beaches

countries.meaning: The Seite Islands bear the turtle of the banks their fathers fished: an isle moot that keeps the reef-shrines, refuses the sea-king every year and knows that its fishers alone cannot hold the banks against his fleet.
countries.blazon: A field divided chevron-wise like a broad roof, chart paper above and chart teal below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A turtle in ink, large in the centre.

countries.name: The Lens

primary_charge.name: a round lens of ground glass
primary_charge.meaning: the lens-grinders (canting on The Lens)

countries.meaning: The Lens bears the great lens of the Lamp-House, the order of glass-blowers sworn after a royal ship was lost on the Cursed Square to keep the northern passages lit for every ship, whatever its flag.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, ink above and chart paper below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A round lens of ground glass in sand gold, outlined in ink, large in the centre.

countries.name: Nondondor

primary_charge.name: a short straight hanger sword
primary_charge.meaning: an isle held by the sword

marks.text: the captain's ring: the isle-lord's charge is set within a plain gold ring

countries.meaning: Nondondor bears the hanger of the captain who beat the corsair captains one by one, within the captain's ring of a sea-king: a kingdom of corsairs and fishers that grants writs or hangs corsairs as suits it and presses the banks claim when its fleet is stronger.
countries.blazon: A plain field of corsair black. A short straight hanger sword in ransom gold, large in the centre. The charge is set within a plain heavy ring of ransom gold.

countries.name: Windy Lands

primary_charge.name: a fishing kite on its line
primary_charge.meaning: the kite-fishers of the windward capes

countries.meaning: The Windy Lands bear three fishing kites for the cape-lords of the windward capes, who fish from kites and take what the storm drives onto their rocks: a league that pays tribute to strong fleets, raids weak ones and never agrees on anything quickly.
countries.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, blood red above and sea ink below, by an indented line of small even teeth. Three of fishing kite on its line, two above one in bone, large in the centre.

countries.name: Santon

primary_charge.name: a ship under a black sail
primary_charge.meaning: the Black Flag Night

countries.meaning: Santon bears the black sail of the captain who took the strait-place harbour of Straton: corsairs in the dead harbours of the outer western arc, who remember that Corogon has sworn to burn Straton again.
countries.blazon: A field divided across, bone above and sea ink below, by an indented line of small even teeth. A ship under a black sail in corsair black, outlined in bone, large in the centre.

countries.name: Benan

primary_charge.name: a cove under a mountain
primary_charge.meaning: the coves no fleet can find without a Benan pilot

countries.meaning: Benan bears the cove under the mountain that no fleet can find without a Benan pilot: the corsair haven of Torni, which takes tribute from the Charter, raids when it is late and keeps well away from the Cursed Square.
countries.blazon: A field divided upright, blood red at the hoist and corsair black at the fly, by an indented line of small even teeth. A cove under a mountain in ransom gold, large in the centre.

engine_facts: Dynamic tags D01 to D75 are a shared pool (zz_zin_dynamic_countries.txt, dynamic_tags = yes); the installed game ships no flag file for them.
start_civil_war and create_dynamic_country both run an effect block on the new country (effects_documentation.md), so every creation site can set_cosmetic_tag there.

A dynamic country keeps original_tag = its parent; ZIN ships no ideology flag variants (asset manifest section 6), so without a cosmetic tag a breakaway would show its parent's flag or the D-tag fallback (probe AP5).
dynamic.rule: Every script that creates a dynamic country sets a cosmetic tag in the same effect block. A story creation uses its named cosmetic tag (story list). Any other creation uses zin_dyn_<PARENT>_<kind> whose design is derived from the parent record and its culture grammar by the algorithm below. The D-tag base files are a fallback the build forbids reaching.

breakaway.when: A civil war breakaway (start_civil_war) or a rebel realm splitting from a parent.
steps: Counterchange the field: swap the order of the two field tinctures; a plain field takes the primary charge's tincture and the charge takes the field's.
Keep the primary charge: the breakaway claims the same realm. Drop the secondary charge.

Add the culture's breakaway mark (difference.breakaway_mark): a border in the culture's line, tinctured with difference.dissent_tincture. A Concord dominion instead shows the charter border broken open at the top; a Free Crown shows its crown torn from the beast; a realm sworn to the Dominion keeps the grave base, which it cannot break.
Keep the family mark (Aen's label, the family line). Never add or remove a people mark.
Apply the ideology overlay of the breakaway's ruling ideology.
Re-run contrast, palette and near-duplicate checks; the derived flag must be at least 10 of 64 from its parent.

released.when: A land given its own realm (create_dynamic_country for a people or province with no tag of its own).
steps: Take the grammar of the released land's majority culture, not the releaser's.
Division: the first entry of the culture's divisions list whose (division, field tinctures) signature is unused in the region.
Field: the first pair of culture tinctures (one metal, one colour) unused with that division in the region.
Primary charge: the first culture charge not used as a primary charge in the region.
Secondary charge: the culture's restoration charge (difference.restoration_charge), small in base: the realm restored.

If the releaser keeps it as a subject, add the releaser's subject mark (charter border of Aenor, grave base of the Dominion, the Iron Yoke of Goldoroth, the ward border of Hirolon or Herrodon, or for any other releaser its dissent tincture as a narrow border).

formed.when: A union of two or more founders (a formable that is created as a dynamic country).
steps: Impale: divide per pale in the family line of the senior founder; the hoist half carries the senior founder's first field tincture and primary charge, the fly half the junior founder's.
With three or more founders, the fly half is the senior culture's darkest colour charged with the junior founders' primary charges small, two above one.
If the formed realm is a kingdom, the senior culture's crown is placed over the line of impalement.
Never quarter more than four pieces and never tierce in three equal upright bands (a real-world tricolour).

democratic.rule: The metal part of the field becomes the culture's lightest metal; no crown is added.

fascism.rule: The culture's crown is added over the charge; a culture without a crown uses a plain circlet in its lightest metal.

communism.rule: The colour part of the field becomes the culture's darkest tincture and the charge its palest; nothing else changes (no new symbols of the dark powers on a mortal realm).

neutrality.rule: Any crown is removed; the counterchanged field stands alone.

story.name: The Golden Court
story.gate: Aenor succession war, court camp (aenor_court_and_succession section 7)
story.blazon: A field divided across, lamp gold above and lake blue below, by a straight line. A great bell in deep lake, outlined in Parim white, large in the centre, under a circlet of five flame-shaped points in deep lake. A plain narrow border of bell bronze.
story.meaning: The court's gold laid over the realm's blue, with Aenor's bell darkened and a bronze border of difference: the party of the gilded halls that sells offices and still claims the crown.

story.name: Aenor of the Faithful
story.gate: Aenor succession war, Faithful camp, before zin_afrit_revealed
story.blazon: A field of Parim white with a base of lake blue edged by a straight line. A round loaf in lamp gold, outlined in deep lake, large in the centre; a great bell in bell bronze, small, beneath it. A plain narrow border of slate.
story.meaning: The loaf of the Houses of the First Light's public charity above Aenor's bell: the camp that puts the faith before the crown. Nothing on it shows who leads the faith.
story.canon_note: Public arms before the reveal: the deny-list of the Worshipdom applies (no eye, chain, ash, mask, veil, serpent, horns, fire-bird, hidden face), and no lamp with an open flame appears (the arms of Lumae of the twelve).

story.name: The Ashen Throne
story.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, slate above and deep lake below, by a straight line. A great bell in Parim white with a crack running down its side, large in the centre, under a circlet of five flame-shaped points in lamp gold.
story.meaning: After the reveal Aenor's bell is cracked: the Concord of Aen's kingdoms broken under a throne it did not choose. The arms say nothing of the power behind the throne.
story.canon_note: Afrit's true nature never appears on public arms (owner, 24 October 2026): no ash, no flame, no eye, no sign of the god-king; the record keeps its cosmetic tag and the name the court mechanic uses.

story.name: The Stranger's Host
story.gate: Aenor succession war, host camp, before zin_eindil_named

primary_charge.name: a wayfarer's staff with a small shuttered lantern hung from its head

story.blazon: A field divided diagonally from the upper hoist corner, Parim white above and lake blue below, by a straight line. A wayfarer's staff bendwise in bell bronze with a small shuttered lantern in lamp gold hung from its head.
story.meaning: A traveller's staff carrying a lantern: the host gathered by a stranger from the north whose name is not yet known; nothing shows his blood.

story.name: The Host of Eindil
story.parent: host realm (SEL, Selen, in the historical path)

primary_charge.name: Aen's label, large, as the whole charge

story.blazon: A plain field of lake blue. Across the upper half a broad label of three square points in Parim white, large. Beneath it a wayfarer's staff in bell bronze with a small shuttered lantern in lamp gold, upright.
story.meaning: The label, every Ainic realm's small mark of descent, becomes the whole charge: the host of the son of Ein, son of Aen, whose claim is the line itself; uncrowned until the realm crowns him.

story.name: The Free Dominions
story.blazon: A plain field of lake blue. In chief a narrow label of three short square points in lamp gold. A closed book with clasps in Parim white, large in the centre. A plain narrow border of lamp gold, broken open at the top.
story.meaning: The Charters of Parim held by the dominions themselves: the charter border broken open at the top where the crown once sealed it, and no crown.

story.name: Aenor (the crowned heir of Aen)
story.blazon: A plain field of lake blue. A great bell in lamp gold, large in the centre, under an ancient plain circlet of pale gold set with one white stone.
story.meaning: Aenor's own arms under the ancient crown of Aen instead of the lamp-crown: the realm restored to the line it was founded by. Glo and the blue sword are not shown (reserved charges).

story.name: The Dominion of the East
story.blazon: A field of hostel white with a chief of pilgrim gold edged by a straight line. A hand from the base offering a round loaf in bread brown, large, under a tall plain crown of bread brown; beside it a pilgrim's staff in sky blue, small.
story.meaning: The pilgrims' charity crowned: the realm proclaimed a kingdom of the East. The arms still show only the public faith and nothing of what leads it.
story.canon_note: No lamp with an open flame (the arms of Lumae of the twelve) and nothing of Afrit; no crown appears before zin_afrit_king_of_east.

story.name: Great Goldoroth
story.blazon: A plain field of ash black. A fire-mountain with a plume of flame in ember orange within a ring of upright stakes in ash grey, large in the centre, under a circlet of upturned tusks in bone.
story.meaning: The Fire-Mountain inside one challenge ring: every hold that bent to the Warking now stands in his ring.

regional_cliches.rule: banned everywhere (the rejected 19 October sheets put palms across the East)
no primary charge more than twice in a region and never twice in a culture; no charge class above 40 percent of a region with ten or more flags
once in all the East Lands (The Moco)
once per region at most (Gord in the Dark Lands); never for corsairs, never for the dead
at most one per culture (the Lands of Light noon-door, the Land of the Sun's sun court)
no masonry, battlements, crenellation, brick courses or wall towers for the Great Wall of Aenor, which is a mountain range
only in a demon sigil, at most one in Aoaz (the Nether)

real_world_flags_and_arms: tricolours: any field of three equal upright or horizontal bands, with or without a charge
stars and stripes: alternating stripes with a canton; stars in a canton or in rows; a ring of stars (including twelve)
crescent and star, a crescent alone
any cross throughout: Nordic (offset), St George, St Andrew saltire, Greek or Latin cross charges, cross pattee, Maltese cross
hammer and sickle, hammer and compasses, crossed tools, cogwheels
eagles in national poses: displayed, double-headed, on a cactus, with a snake

a lion rampant of national type, three lions passant, a rose of the Tudor kind, a fleur-de-lis, a maple leaf, a cedar of the Lebanese kind, a harp of the Irish kind, a red dragon on green and white, a dragon on a diagonal bicolour
a red disc on white; a rising sun with rays to the edges; a sun with a face; a sun over waves; a canoe over a sun over waves; a frigate bird over a sun
a large plain disc or lozenge on a plain field (Japan, Bangladesh, Brazil types)
a yurt roof-wheel, a spoked wheel of eight or twenty-four spokes
a skull and crossbones, a fouled anchor, a compass rose of four points
chequy red and white, lozengy blue and white, gold with red pales, gyronny gold and black (Croatian, Bavarian, Aragonese, Campbell arms)
real_religious_symbols: star of David or any hexagram
pentagram and inverted pentagram (except a pentagram inside a demon sigil, owner 24 October 2026; never a cross of any arrangement, inverted or upright)
ichthys, chalice, dove with olive branch, lamb with banner
eye of Horus, winged sun disc
other_fiction: a white tree with stars and crown
a direwolf, kraken, three-headed dragon, sun pierced by a spear, golden rose on green
forbidden.lettering: No letters, numerals, runes, monograms, mottoes, signatures or maker's marks anywhere on a flag.
forbidden.owner_emblem: Never the owner's ZIN emblem: a square frame with its two diagonals crossed and an upright staff through the centre; no square frame with crossed diagonals in any arms.
names_and_canon: no named New God charge and no god's device (pantheon.json symbols: Glernaen, Sulethe, Lumae, Maelwen, Vaelei, Rasthel, Kerun, Aurlan, Ailtal, Irumas, Gaelor and Naisa have names and arms; no national flag shows them)
no figure of Zol, Volgan, Afrit, Elzon, Horos or any named person
no Afrit or Hidden Council sign on the Worshipdom or Aenor public arms (deny-list in the Worshipdom record); Afrit's true nature never appears on public arms, before or after the reveal
Zol's servant (Kusven, formerly Edvoid) never appears on any flag, nor his dwelling of the black oval; Zol's Mistake shows only its emblem leader's sigil, the Will of Zol
Glo, Horos's blue sword and its shards are reserved charges: owner approval and a story gate are required
no device of Elzon's Order (the Pale Regency) on any living realm
nothing of the wider world (Erdu, Dunda, Haven, Cerio, Lao and the small neighbouring continent)

checks.coverage: every realm of roster.json (156 tags) and D01-D75 in common/country_tags, and every cosmetic tag in common/countries/cosmetic.txt, has a design record and gfx/flags/<TAG>.tga, medium/<TAG>.tga and small/<TAG>.tga; no flag file without a tag

headers.measured_from: installed game gfx/flags/FRA_democratic.tga, medium/FRA_democratic.tga, small/GER.tga and small/FRA.tga (24 October 2026)

checks.palette_fit: k-means on the 82x52 image with k = declared tinctures + 1; every cluster above 6 percent of pixels lies within Delta E 2000 of 12 of a declared tincture of the record (culture palette, declared borrowings, overlord marks)
checks.contrast: primary charge tincture against each field tincture it overlaps: luminance ratio at least 2.2, or the record declares fimbriation
checks.element_budget: marks plus charges at most 4 (5 is a hard failure)
checks.small_signature: (division, field tinctures) unique within a region; the mean Delta E 2000 of the approximate 3x2 small-flag grid between any two flags of a region at least 6 on the records, and at least 10 on the generated 10x7 images
checks.unique_design: design_hash (division, line, field, primary, secondary, marks) unique across all records

near_duplicate.hash: 64-bit difference hash (grey 9x8) and 64-bit average hash; distance = larger Hamming distance
near_duplicate.real_world_reference: computed at build time, read-only, from every flag of the installed game gfx/flags (a corpus of real national flags of the 1930s); nothing is copied or stored
near_duplicate.colour_grid: 3x2 mean colour grid; a pair closer than 10 hashes is also compared by grid, mean Delta E 2000 under 18 fails

checks.forbidden_text: record blazons and prompts are scanned for the forbidden vocabulary; the generated large sheet gets an OCR pass that must find no glyphs
checks.canon_gates: reserved charges only in gated records; the Worshipdom and Aenor public arms pass the hidden-identity deny-list
checks.provenance: each sheet has one line in art/source/provenance.jsonl (id, prompt, prompt sha256, record design_hash list, reference images, output, output sha256, review); each flag file has a line in art/source/flags_manifest.json (source sheet, cell, crop box, operations, output sha256)

design_distance.rule: distance over division (3, or 1 for the line alone), field tinctures (1.5 each, scaled by Delta E 2000 over 25), primary charge (4 for another class, 3 for another charge of the class), primary tincture (1, scaled), count (1), secondary charge (2) and marks (0.5 each); any pair of country or story designs below the minimum fails

checks.god_devices: no country or story record reproduces the device of a named god of pantheon.json (an eye, a brimming bowl, a lamp with an open flame, waves under a cloud, a ring with a shoot, a gate with a staff, a tower on a mount, a sheaf under rain, a bound standing stone, an anvil, a furled sail, a star) and no record names a god

pipeline.grouping: sheets are filled in order family, culture, region, tag, so one sheet carries one family's grammar; a sheet never mixes the dead or demons with living cultures
pipeline.prompt_frame:
A flat asset sheet of {n} distinct heraldic flags for a medieval-fantasy strategy game, arranged in an exact {cols} columns by {rows} rows grid. The background is solid flat pure black (#000000) everywhere between and around the flags: no glow, no blur, no gradient, no texture. Every flag is a perfectly flat, front-facing rectangle with an aspect ratio of 41 to 26, all the same size, evenly spaced with identical black gutters; no perspective, no waving, no folds, no shadows, no frames, no poles. Painted heraldic style: flat tinctures exactly as named, bold silhouettes with a thin dark outline, a faint woven-cloth texture inside each flag, no gradients, no fine detail smaller than one fortieth of the flag's height. No lettering, no letters, numbers or runes anywhere; no signature or maker's mark; corners and bottom edge hold only plain ground; no real-world religious symbol; no real national flag or coat of arms; no crosses, stars, crescents or eagles; no masonry or battlements. {family_style}
{rows_text}
pipeline.family_style: Family style: {family.mark_text}. Shared palette of this sheet: {palette names}.
pipeline.reference: after the first accepted sheet, the job passes that sheet as a layout-only reference ("copy its black background, grid, flag size and spacing exactly; copy none of its designs")
slicing: Find the 12 flag rectangles by the black-gutter layout check (existing flag-jobs check: expected count, columns, rows, aspect 1.4 to 1.75).
Inset each rectangle by 2 percent on every side to drop edge fringe.
Medium: Lanczos-3 resize of the inset source to 41x26.
Small: box-filter (area) downscale of the inset source to 10x7; this squeezes the 41:26 artwork horizontally as the game's own small flags do.
Write uncompressed 32-bit TGA, bottom-left origin, alpha 255, descriptor as measured (0x08 large and medium, 0x00 small).
No recolouring, palette snapping or redrawing: if a size fails a check, the sheet is regenerated.
